" KB0014789 Printers/Fax/Other Devices What is the Mail Relay Service? "
Technologies such as printers, routers, cloud vendors, and HVAC systems sometimes need to send email, but they generally cannot use Rutgers Connect or ScarletMail. In order to support these products, the Office of Information Technology (OIT) offers a portfolio of mail relay services. 
Access to these services comes via application. 
Commonly Accepted Usages 	Commonly Excluded Usages 
•	Networked printers (e.g. toner/paper notification email)
•	Switches/routers (e.g. operational email) 
•	Automated HVAC systems 
•	Emergency generators (e.g. fuel status email) 
•	Software performing “basic authentication” (i.e. authentication is not performed via OAuth or a similar modern protocol). This software is incompatible with Rutgers cloud email providers. 
•	Products that are unable to use a password when sending email. 	•	Individual email accounts/aliases 
•	Usage from individual computers that can be performed using Outlook, webmail, etc. 
•	Products not able to perform email encryption (e.g. SSL or TLS) 
•	Service to shared infrastructure; for example, to an outside vendor that cannot ensure exclusive Rutgers resources. 
•	Usage by non-Rutgers affiliates 
Software/applications running on dedicated servers, virtual appliances, and vendor-provided IT services will be considered on a case-by-case basis with consideration to the applicable policies and guidelines. The platform should be formally procured by Rutgers and use appropriate measures that ensure Rutgers IT resources are only provided for Rutgers related usage. To confirm compatibility, you are encouraged to engage OIT promptly whenever email integrations are required. 
Available Services
OIT currently offers four classes of mail relay service. The request process will guide you to a suggested offering. If you have an explicit service requirement, please note that during the request process. 
•	SMTP AUTH mail sending service: A special NetID and password, allocated to your service and not any one person, is created for your request. Please note that this service requires the security of TLS or SSL encryption. Email may be sent as any authorized Rutgers-affiliated email address. 
•	IMAP or POP3 mail receiving service: A special NetID and password, allocated to your service and not any one person, is created for your request. A mailbox is created for that special NetID, which will receive email for retrieval (via IMAP or POP3) under the security of TLS encryption. Your Rutgers Connect domain administrator may create an alias, in Rutgers Connect, that will “hide” the special NetID for marketing purposes. (If the special NetID will only be used by automated processes, a marketing alias is not required.)
•	SMTP AUTH with IMAP or SMTP AUTH with POP3: If there is a requirement to both send and receive email, this offering is a combination of offerings #1 and #2.
•	IP-based mail sending service: The IP address of your University-affiliated device will be permitted to send email, using SMTP, as any authorized Rutgers-affiliated email address. This is the only offering available for devices that cannot ensure the security of a Rutgers NetID and password — for example, devices that cannot support encryption. This offering is generally restricted to RUNet-connected devices.
Request Process
Mail relay privileges can be requested by the appropriate Administrative or Technical Contact for the device by logging into the request webtool: Request Mail Relay Access
Upon submitting a completed online application, the request will be assessed, and its status communicated via email. All accepted and rejected submissions will be acknowledged via email to the submitter. Rejected submissions may also include details on reasons for the rejection and corrective actions which must be taken prior to resubmission. 
Exclusions and Audits
Exemption from NetID authentication does not constitute exemption from the relevant University policies, guidelines, and technical standards. If a device is found in violation, mail relay permission may be denied and/or revoked. Generally, we will first attempt to remedy this situation with the contacts listed on the application. 
OIT reserves the right to conduct audits of devices with mail relay permission. Timely responses to OIT audits are mandatory for continued permission to utilize Rutgers services. 
If a device is excluded, OIT must receive verification that the conditions that led to the device’s exclusion have been corrected and verified prior to reinstatement. 
For more information on the standards of data protection required of authorized devices, please visit Information Security Cybersecurity Compliance Program.

" KB0016525 Printing (with PaperCut) How to allow PaperCut to scan to your OneDrive "
The scanning feature available in PaperCut allows you to send or save scanned documents to various destinations, including cloud storage. 
You must go through the scanning process to generate an email with instructions to allow PaperCut to save scanned documents to your OneDrive. This email will contain a link that asks you to log in to OneDrive for Business to do a one-time authorization of the Scans for PaperCut MF application to send files to your OneDrive for Business account. This authorization link is valid for 24 hours; after this time, the scanned document will be automatically deleted. Once authorized, access remains valid for 90 days after your last scanned document is saved to OneDrive. If you are scanning to your OneDrive more than 90 days after you last did, you will have to go through this authorization process again. 

Please note that all emails sent from the PaperCut system will be sent to your netid@rutgers.edu email address. If you are unsure if your netid@rutgers.edu address delivers to Rutgers Connect or ScarletMail, go to the Manage Email Addresses page, and check the delivery location under Delivery Addresses for Personalized Email Addresses.
1.	You will need to create a scanned document following the instructions on how to scan to OneDrive on PaperCut.

     Error! Filename not specified.

     Error! Filename not specified.

" KB0016529 Printing (with PaperCut) PaperCut Scan to OneDrive FAQ "
Table of Contents
•	Who has access to "Scan to OneDrive" at the University?
•	How do I allow PaperCut to saved scanned document files to my OneDrive?
•	Where are scanned documents saved in OneDrive by default? Can this default location be changed?
•	Can the filename of the scanned document be changed?
•	Can I change my e-mail address that is used for receiving scanned documents via email?
•	I have already allowed PaperCut to save scanned documents to my OneDrive. Why have I received another email asking me to allow this access?
Who has access to Scan to OneDrive at the University?
While Scan to OneDrive will be listed as a scan option for all PaperCut users, only users who have access to OneDrive on Rutgers Connect will be able to save scanned documents to OneDrive. This includes:
•	
o	Students
o	Faculty
o	Staff
There are roles within the University that do not receive Rutgers Connect access by default but can be granted access with local IT approval. These roles include:
•	
o	Emeritus
o	Guest
Also, there are some roles within the University that are not granted Rutgers Connect access and, therefore, would not be able to save scanned documents to OneDrive. These include:
•	
o	Alumni
o	Retiree
Please note that a person can have multiple roles with the University, and if they are assigned at least one role that is granted Rutgers Connect access, they will be able to save scanned documents to OneDrive.  For example, someone who is an Alumni and a Staff member would be granted access to saved scanned documents to OneDrive via their Staff role.
How do I allow PaperCut to save scanned document files to my OneDrive?
The first time you scan to your OneDrive, you'll need to follow the instructions to allow Papercut access to your OneDrive. 
Where are scanned documents saved in OneDrive by default? Can this default location be changed?
The default location in your OneDrive is under My Files > Apps > Scans for PaperCut MF. This default location cannot be changed. However, you can move the scanned document file to any other folder once it has been saved to your OneDrive.
Can the filename of the scanned document be changed?
The filename of the scanned document can be changed during the scanning process while using the multi-function printer. If you tap the filename, a touchscreen keyboard should appear to let you edit the filename:
     Error! Filename not specified.

Please note that when saving scanned documents to OneDrive, you could experience issues if you happen to re-use the name of a scanned document that already exists in the destination.  If you still would like to change the name of the scanned document, here are some suggestions to avoid these issues:
•	
o	Leave the filename generated by PaperCut during the scan process, which contains a timestamp to help avoid duplicate names. The scanned document can be renamed once it arrives in your OneDrive.
o	Edit the filename, but leave the timestamp portion of the generated document name, guaranteeing that a file of the same name doesn't already exist in OneDrive.
Can I change the email address I use to receive scanned documents via email?
All emails sent from the PaperCut system will be sent to your netid@rutgers.edu email address. If you are unsure if your netid@rutgers.edu address delivers to Rutgers Connect or ScarletMail, go to the Manage Email Addresses page, and check the delivery location under Delivery Addresses for Personalized Email Addresses.
I have already allowed PaperCut to save scanned documents to my OneDrive. Why have I received another email asking me to allow this access?
If you haven't saved a scan to your OneDrive in the past 90 days, the authorization token created during the initial confirmation process will expire. You'll need to follow the instructions to allow PaperCut access to your OneDrive to create a new authorization.
" KB0016057 Printing (with PaperCut) Poster printing in the OIT computing labs "
OIT offers three wide-width printers (plotters) for poster printing.
Location
One is located in the College Ave Computer Center in the Academic Building on College Avenue, another is in the Allison Road Classroom Computing Lab on Busch, and an additional one is in the Loree Computing Lab on Cook/Douglass. Poster printers are not available on the Livingston campus. 
Cost
The cost for printing is $1.50 per square foot. For example, a 3ft x 2ft poster would cost $9.00. 
Supported File Types
You can use several software programs to print to the plotter, but Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Adobe applications are most commonly used. The plotters work with files that are .doc, .pdf, .ppt, or .tiff; however, .pdf is the recommended file type. 
Please ensure the size of the printed file is not too large. File sizes of 200MB or greater may cause issues where the print job will not appear when you go to get the print released. If the file size is large (exceeds 100MB), please try flattening the PDF using Adobe Photoshop or the images used within the poster. If the original PDF width and height don't match the sizes mentioned below in the Available Sizes section, please use Photoshop to resize the dimensions of the PDF. You can flatten or resize PDFs in Photoshop by doing the following:
1.	Open Photoshop and select New File to create a new document.
2.	Set the Width and Height corresponding to the poster size you will be printing. 
o	For example, if printing for size E, you would set Width to 34 Inches and Height to 44 Inches.
3.	Set the Resolution to 300 Pixels/Inch.
4.	Select Create to create the document.
5.	Select File > Open... and open the PDF that needs to be flattened or size-adjusted. 
o	This PDF should open in a secondary tab next to the Untitled-1 document you created.
6.	Select the whole PDF using Ctrl + A.
7.	Switch to the Untitled-1 document you created, and paste what you copied using Ctrl + V.
8.	Resize, rotate, and adjust the pasted content as needed using Ctrl + T to enable transform mode.
9.	Press the checkmark icon in the top bar or Enter, to finalize the transformation.
10.	Select File > Save as... and change the Save as type to Photoshop PDF.
11.	Select Save to save the PDF, then use this instead of the original large file size or an incorrectly-dimensioned PDF.
Available Sizes
The plotter is set to print predetermined sizes, which are depicted by letters in the print options. Print time ranges from 1 to 3 minutes, depending on the size chosen. 
•	A (Letter): 8.5 x 11 inches ~ $0.97
•	B (Tabloid): 11 x17 inches ~ $1.95
•	C: 17 x 22 inches ~ $3.90
•	D: 22 x 34 inches ~ $7.79
•	E: 34 x 44 inches ~ $15.58
 
     Error! Filename not specified.

" KB0012627 Printing (with PaperCut) "Printing overview for Students, Faculty and Staff" "
Printing is available for Students, Faculty, and Staff at the Office of Information Technology computer labs. You may print to black-and-white or color printers from lab computers, wirelessly via personal devices on RUWirelessSecure, or through Virtual Computer Labs.
You must release the print jobs via the print release stations in each computer lab printing location in Rutgers–New Brunswick, Rutgers–Newark, and Rutgers–Camden. Your RUID card is required to release print jobs. 
Printing rates
There will be no charge for the first $30 of printing that each individual releases during every six-month printing period (January to June; July to December). The $30 allocation is the same for all Students, Faculty, and Staff, regardless of the details of their academic and university arrangements (e.g., number of credits, part-time vs. full-time status, etc.). Rates for printing are as follows:
•	$.04 per sheet for black and white printing
•	$.25 per sheet for color printing
Please note that the $30 allocation is equivalent to:
•	750 sheets in black and white, OR
•	120 sheets in color, OR
•	any combination thereof
Remember, single-sided and double-sided sheets have the same rates, so everyone is encouraged to always print double-sided, which is the default setting on most Office of Information Technology lab computers.
Checking your print balance and adding funds
To check your print balance, visit the PaperCut website and enter your NetID and password. Note that to access this remotely, you will need to log in to the VPN first.
For individuals affiliated with Rutgers Health Sciences (RBHS), Rutgers–New Brunswick, or Rutgers–Camden, once your funds have depleted, further charges will be deducted from your RU Express account. If you need to add funds, you can do so through the RUExpress account website.
For individuals affiliated with Rutgers–Newark, further charges would be deducted from your Raider Dollar Account. If you need to add funds to your Raider Dollar Account, you can do so online using the Newark eAccounts website.
Have issues printing?
If you encounter issues printing, speak with a consultant in that specific computer lab.
Additional information
To learn more about the printing processes at an OIT computer lab, please visit the PaperCut knowledge base.
" KB0013020 Privacy and security FAQ for ScarletApps Are there specific risks due to some of Google's servers being hosted in other countries? "
By law, some intellectual property should not be stored outside of the United States. Individuals handling sensitive materials are reminded not to share this information via email regardless of the email provider.
Ultimately, an email that is intended for a user within the U.S. can be easily forwarded.
" KB0013023 Privacy and security FAQ for ScarletApps How does Google address privacy and security? "
Google is very concerned about the security and privacy of its users' data. Please see Google’s Privacy Policy.
Google provides information regarding how to stay safe online, how to manage your data, and the safety of your data on the web and on Google. Visit Google’s Safety Center for more information. 
" KB0013019 Privacy and security FAQ for ScarletApps How does ScarletMail handle spam and viruses? "
Google filters for viruses and spam before delivering the message. For more information, please see Google’s information on spam filters.
" KB0013021 Privacy and security FAQ for ScarletApps Is email a secure form of communication? "
Sensitive information should NEVER be sent through email. We advise against sending sensitive information via email for the following reasons:
•	Email could be intercepted and accessed by an unauthorized party
•	Email could be shared inappropriately by the recipient
•	Email could be compromised for as long as it is retained by you or the recipient
•	There are no retention controls over the recipient’s system
•	Accessing your email over an insecure network (i.e., Internet Cafe or open wireless network) can expose your user account information
•	Although encrypted connections can mitigate the risks of having ones’ authentication credentials compromised, email itself is still plain text when traveling between the sender and the recipient and can be easily intercepted
Regardless of the provider, email is not a secure method of communication. This applies to our current campus email systems as well as most third-party email providers.
" KB0013022 Privacy and security FAQ for ScarletApps Some of my ScarletMail emails contain confidential material. How will you maintain email privacy? "
Confidential or sensitive information should NEVER be sent through email.
Google maintains Privacy Policies for each of its applications. For a complete list and access to each of these policies, please visit Google’s Privacy Center.
" KB0013016 Privacy and security FAQ for ScarletApps What are the Policies or Terms of Service for the Google products and services I use? "
All of the products, applications, and services used in the ScarletApps at Rutgers environment are subject to the Rutgers University Acceptable Use Policy and Google’s Terms of Service for that product.
Individual products, applications, and services may have supplemental terms of service applied in addition to Google’s general Terms of Service. These supplemental terms of service can most often be found by selecting the link on the bottom of the page for that product under Terms and Policies.
If there is ever a conflict between Google’s Terms of Service and the Rutgers AUP, the Rutgers AUP takes precedent.
" KB0013024 Privacy and security FAQ for ScarletApps What constitutes sensitive information in the context of electronic communications? "
Sensitive information is information such as Social Security numbers, driver license numbers, credit card information, medical/health conditions, etc. None of this information should be sent via email, regardless of the email provider. As a general rule, privacy experts advise to consider whether it would be appropriate or desirable for the contents of the email to appear in a public forum (e.g., newspaper). Email operates as a postcard that can easily be read in transit and at the destination by unauthorized parties. It could be retained forever, or shared with unintended readers. For more information, please visit the Rutgers Information Classification Policy and Data Breach Management Policy. 
" KB0013027 Privacy and security FAQ for ScarletApps What is the ScarletMail name policy? "
Use your common first and last name. Impersonation is a serious issue. Pretending to be someone else could cause your profile to be deleted.
Follow Google's guide on how to change your Google account picture, name and other info.
Misrepresenting a user’s identity in any electronic communication is against Rutgers' Acceptable Use Policy.
" KB0013026 Privacy and security FAQ for ScarletApps Who owns the intellectual property rights? "
Although data will be stored by Google, Rutgers retains all intellectual property rights of its data.
" KB0013025 Privacy and security FAQ for ScarletApps Will my personal information from ScarletApps be shared with anyone outside of Rutgers? "
Please refer to Google’s Privacy Policy for more information.

Course Preparation Timeline
4 – 5 Months Before Class Start
•	Log in to the MyRutgers campus portal.
•	In the My Apps tab, use the Bookstore Adoptions (AIP) app to formally adopt your textbook.
•	Contact your Rutgers bookstore manager or your publisher representative to let them know that you would like your course section(s) to participate in First Day.
4 – 6 Weeks Before Class Starts
•	If using publisher courseware (i.e., MyLab, Connect, MindTap), be sure the publisher link is added in your Canvas course site and that you have completed all course setup/pairing. For each publisher, view the Canvas External Apps page for information on enabling the content in your Canvas course. 
•	Ensure that the First Day Course Materials link is visible to students in your First Day courses by enabling it in your course navigation (See Canvas External Tool Configuration).
2 Weeks Before Class Starts
•	Ensure messaging is added to your syllabus and Canvas course that describes the program and its benefits. (See Sample Student Messaging.)
•	Share the Welcome Email (provided by your Bookstore Manager) with your students.
First Day of Class
•	Let students know about this program, which will save them money on their course materials!
•	Ensure students know they can opt out in Canvas via the First Day Course Materials link.
•	Direct any student concerns or questions to the Rutgers Campus bookstore or the Barnes & Noble College Customer Care team, and provide students with the Customer Care Contact Information in this article.
Canvas External Tool Configuration
As an instructor for a First Day™/Inclusive Access course, you will need to add the First Day Course Materials link in Canvas so that students can opt out of the program, if they wish, during the opt-out period only. If the material is an eTextbook only, students can also access their titles at this link.
Steps
1.	Log in to Canvas with your instructor username and password and navigate to the course site that requires the First Day Course Materials link.
2.	Click Settings from the left-hand course navigation.
3.	Click the Navigation tab, and scroll down to the hidden items at the bottom of the list.
4.	Look for the First Day Course Materials in the list.
5.	Click and hold First Day Course Materials, then drag it up to the list of active navigation links, or select the three dots next to the tool and choose Enable.
6.	Click Save.
7.	The First Day Course Materials link will now be available in the left-hand navigation of your course. You may have to refresh your window to see it.
8.	Repeat these steps for any additional Canvas course sites that require the First Day Course Materials link.
Setup First Day Course Materials Link Tutorial
     
First Day™ Faculty Add Course Materials Link – Canvas from Barnes & Noble College on Vimeo.
Managing First Day Course Materials for Cross-listed Sections
Before cross-listing your Canvas course sections, course instructors must follow the Canvas External Tool Configuration steps outlined above for each course site to activate First Day, ensuring that all students in your merged course site have access to your course materials.
 
If any sections of a cross-listed site don't appear in First Day, please try the steps below to have all sections appear.
1.	Contact the Canvas Help Desk and request that your course site be decross-listed.
2.	Add First Day to each section individually.
3.	Recross-list all sections. If the course material was previously imported, ensure the cross-listed course uses the same bucket course.
Sample Student Messaging
To enhance your learning experience and provide affordable access to the right course material, this course is part of an inclusive access model called First Day™. You can easily access the required materials for this course at a discounted price and benefit from single sign-on in Canvas with no codes required.
Rutgers University will bill you at the discounted price as a course charge for these course materials.
It is NOT recommended that you opt out, as these materials are required to complete the course. You can opt out on the first day of class, but you will be responsible for purchasing your course materials at full retail price, and access to your materials may be suspended.
For more information and FAQs, go to Barnes & Noble Customer Care.

" KB0016432 Publishers & Textbooks Library Tutorials – An Introduction for Instructors "
Many college students arrive on campus without essential information skills, creating gaps between faculty expectations and student ability. Our tutorials help bring them up to speed in a convenient, easy-to-use format.
Table of Contents
•	What is this content? 
o	On-Demand Lessons
o	Master Courses
•	Who can use this content, and who is providing it?
•	When can I use the lessons in my course?
•	How will these skills help my students succeed?
•	Which Library Tutorial do I use?
•	Who do I contact for more information?
What is this content?
Our tutorials are high-quality, standards-driven learning objects designed to introduce students to the basics of locating, evaluating, and using information. They include video lessons as well as quizzes to assess understanding.
Tutorials let you focus precious classroom time on your course material rather than research skills. Your students can return to these activities for easy reference throughout the semester.
On-Demand Lessons
On-demand lessons for easy access to our most frequently requested topics:
•	Types of sources
•	Refining search results
•	How to read scholarly materials
•	Academic integrity
•	What is plagiarism?
•	Why citations matter
•	Citation style guides
•	Copyright
•	And more!
Master Courses
These tutorials provide comprehensive deep-dives that can be embedded directly into Canvas:
•	Communication, for increasing the effectiveness of oral, written, and visual communication
•	Critical Thinking, for developing the ability to evaluate, analyze, and synthesize information
•	Health Science, for building skills to locate health resources, apply appropriate research methods, and participate in evidence-based practice
•	Information Literacy, for building skills to locate, cite, manage, and ethically use information
The lessons are mapped to instructional standards, including the Association of American Colleges and Universities (AAC&U VALUE) Rubrics for Information and Literacy and others, the Association of College and Research Libraries (ACRL) Framework for Information Literacy, and the ACRL Visual Literacy Standards.
Who can use this content, and who is providing it?
The Scholarly Information Tutorials content is provided by the Rutgers University Libraries through licenses with Weave and Credo Reference, two leading library instruction providers, for use by Rutgers University instructors on all campuses.
When can I use the lessons in my course?
Tutorials are available as both on-demand lessons that can be accessed on the Libraries’ website and master courses that can be embedded directly into Canvas.
•	As a flipped classroom or to prepare for specialized library instruction: Assigning students to view a video or work through a lesson before they attend a specialized library instruction class can encourage more productive class time.
•	At various points during a scaffolded assignment: Rather than introducing students to multiple concepts at once, you may want to deploy them to students at various points in their process. If you have scaffolded an assignment, with milestones such as a research question, topic choice, working thesis, or annotated bibliography, consider having students review individual lessons as they begin that particular component of the assignment. Quizzes associated with many of the lessons will help you assess their understanding of a particular aspect of research or information literacy concepts.
•	In a first-year or transition class: Many of the lessons can help students appreciate the big-picture importance of information literacy, strong research and evaluation, and communication skills. You may want to select these lessons at the beginning of a unit or as one component of their success in a first-year experience course.
•	At the beginning of a major project: Students may be overwhelmed at the beginning of a major project and not know where to get started. The multimedia lessons cover a wide range of topics essential to success in research, from choosing a topic to evaluating sources.
•	At the point of need: Your students may be working on an assignment independently, but you want them to have access to resources that can help them throughout the research process as needed, such as a tutorial on database searching when they are in the process of finding sources, or a video about the citation style they need to use.
How will these skills help my students succeed?
•	Getting Started with Research – Introduce your students to the basics of conducting research, from selecting appropriate sources to refining search results.
•	Presenting Research and Data – Empower students to communicate their findings effectively in papers and presentations.
•	Academic Integrity – Help your students use information ethically by understanding plagiarism and copyright.
•	Writing and Citing – Step-by-step guides to citing in AMA, APA, Chicago, and MLA styles.
Research has found that students who receive information literacy instruction have higher retention rates and GPAs, as well as successfully complete more credit hours per year than peers who did not receive such instruction (Greater Western Library Alliance, “The Impact of Information Literacy Instruction on Student Success: A Multi-Institutional Investigation and Analysis,” 2017).
Library tutorials help prepare students with the skills they need to successfully evaluate information both inside and outside the classroom.
Which Library Tutorial do I use?
The tutorials are ideal for undergraduate students who need an introduction to the foundations of scholarly research or for anyone who wants to brush up on the key skills needed to successfully accomplish any research-based project.
Your library liaison can help you select the most relevant lessons for your course.
Who do I contact for more information?
For questions about the Library Tutorials content or to supplement the online instruction, please contact the Rutgers Libraries Instructional Support Team.
•	Library Tutorials: Documentation and Resources
•	Library Tutorials in Canvas
" KB0016433 Publishers & Textbooks Library Tutorials – Instructor Quick Start Guide "
The following are items to do or consider doing when setting up a Library Tutorial course for use:
•	Each assignment (e.g., lesson, quiz, activity) in the course is unpublished (i.e., in a draft state). Once you have imported the course, please review all the content and publish the assignments that you would like your students to see.
•	Each assignment has been set up with 0 points. To make an assignment required or to include quiz assessments in your course grade, you will need to change the points and due date. If you would like to set the point value and make other edits, such as setting due dates and assignment availability, edit the assignment. You may change the assignment group according to your course assignment breakdown as described in your syllabus.
•	You are encouraged to move the assignments to the appropriate modules in your course so that they work cohesively with your topics. Change the order of the assignments to align with your syllabus.
•	There are four citation styles addressed in the Information Literacy course. If only certain styles are appropriate for your discipline, you are free to select and publish the assignments for just those styles if you wish.
It is recommended that you work with instructional support from the Rutgers Libraries when importing content to your course.

" KB0018272 Qualtrics Securing Qualtrics Surveys "
Any survey is susceptible to spam from Bots or other unwanted responses. Qualtrics has several tools available to help prevent these instances from compromising your survey and possibly skewing your data. 
Recommended minimum security settings
Captcha Verification
In captcha verification, the respondent is presented with a picture (or “challenge”) of words or characters, and the respondent must correctly type out those characters to proceed. This is especially important for surveys using a single link that allows anyone to take the survey anonymously. 
Survey Availability
With the survey availability setting, you can make your survey available until a set expiration date when the survey will be closed to new respondents. This is vital to ensuring surveys do not continue collecting responses long after the survey should have ended. 
Securing your Survey
Securing how someone accesses your survey is always an essential first step. These options can increase your survey’s security and help protect it from unwanted responses. Detailed instructions on enabling these features can be found on the Qualtrics Support page for Security Surveys Options. 
Survey Access
There are two ways a respondent can enter your survey. The first is to do so anonymously by clicking an anonymous link. The second, more secure way, is to click a unique link generated for specific individuals.
Password Protection
You can set a single, general password that any respondent must enter to access your survey. This is helpful when using the anonymous link and restricting who can enter the survey. 
Add a Referral Website URL
Specify the URL your respondents must come from to access your survey. This setting is useful if your survey link is posted on a particular website.
Prevent Indexing
Search engines create an index, or a map of all pages on the Internet, so they can be searched quickly. This keeps search engines from finding and presenting your survey in their search results.
Spam and Fraud Detection
In addition to securing your survey, it is recommended that you take further action to prevent bots or malicious actors from skewing your data. Detailed instructions on enabling these features can be found on the Qualtrics Support page for Fraud Detection. 
Prevent Multiple Submissions
This works by placing a cookie on the respondent's browser when they submit a response. The next time they click the survey link, Qualtrics will see this cookie and not permit them to take the survey again.
Bot detection
Every response is rated on the probability that the respondent was a bot, and their responses are flagged accordingly. 
Security Scan Monitor
Prevent email scanning software from inadvertently starting a survey session when a survey link is included in an email.
RelevantID
Analyze a respondent’s browser, operating system, and location to determine the likelihood that the same respondent is answering repeatedly.
" KB0013334 Qualtrics Sharing or Utilizing Groups for Qualtrics Surveys "
The use of the Qualtrics collaboration feature is always recommended prior to creating a Group since it is entirely controlled by you with no outside assistance needed and serves the purpose in most cases. Groups can be created, if necessary, but are subject to the process listed below anytime a change is required.
Collaboration
This is the recommended method of sharing a survey with another person. The collaboration feature allows you to give other people with Qualtrics accounts access to your surveys when they log into their accounts. That way, you can work on the same project without giving out your account information. You can even choose to restrict what type of access other people have to your project.
Groups
Groups allow you to work as a team with a shared library to store survey templates, contact lists, etc... Groups can only be created and managed by a Qualtrics Brand Administrator. 
Creating a new group
To request a group be created, send an email to qualtrics_support@oit.rutgers.edu and include:
•	Your name and NetID.
•	Brief, yet descriptive, name for the Group.
•	Names and NetIDs of the users they want to add to the group. They must have a Rutgers Qualtrics account already in order to be added.
Updating group membership

•	Your name and NetID
•	Name of the Group

Steps you will need to take to ensure your users can access their desktops via the Microsoft Remote Desktop Gateway Service.
Infrastructure
•	All hardware and host-based Firewalls will need to be configured to allow RDP Access from the Gateway Servers on the following networks (172.29.207.96/27) and (10.81.67.0/24).
•	The Current configuration of the RD Gateway is only set up for the standard RDP port: 3389
•	If you wish to use a non-standard port for your RDP traffic, please contact the EI Windows Team at ei_windows@oit.rutgers.edu and submit the ports you wish to use.
Local Machines

1.

2.	Run: %windir%\System32\SystemPropertiesRemote.exe

4.	Check the box for Allow connections only from computers running Remote Desktop with Network Level Authentication.
5.	Click on Select Users. 

     Error! Filename not specified.

     Error! Filename not specified.

" KB0015731 Remote Desktop Services RBHS Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) Gateway access "
Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) Gateway provides RDP access to on-campus Windows desktops from external networks without requiring a Virtual Private Network (VPN). Once connected, you can access everything on your computer and on the network. Contact your local IT group to configure your PC to allow Remote Desktop connections.
Key factors to consider:
•	Rutgers Biomedical and Health Sciences (RBHS) staff must first complete VPN registration before configuring their RBHS desktop to allow Remote Desktop connections and permit traffic through local firewalls.
•	Contact your IT Team and confirm that your machine and network are enabled for the RD Gateway.
•	Speak with your IT Team to learn more about department-specific policies regarding the Remote access of University Owned Equipment and resources.
•	Before you can remotely connect to your machine, you will need a NetID and Password, and either the IP Address or Machine Name of the Remote Desktop.
•	This process is only compatible with two-step users configured to use the mobile app. It is not compatible with SMS or hardware tokens.
•	Follow the instructions to setup your Two-step login and devices with DUO, or use the VPN to access your devices.

" KB0012481 ResNet Support "Connect your smart devices, streaming devices, gaming consoles, and desktops" "
Table of Contents

•	Supported devices
To connect your laptop, phone, or tablet to the wireless network for use across all Rutgers buildings, reference the instructions on how to connect to RUWireless Secure. 
Game consoles, smart TVs, streaming devices, some smart devices, and wired (Ethernet) desktops can be connected to the Rutgers Residential Network (ResNet), which is available only in the residence halls.
Anyone connecting to the Rutgers Network must follow the Rutgers Acceptable Use Policy for Computing and Information Technology Resources [PDF]. If you are caught violating this policy, your connection may be terminated without warning.
Wireless Devices
To connect devices wirelessly, such as Google Home, Amazon Echo, gaming consoles, smart devices, etc, you will need to generate your own unique Passphrase, which is your password to use on the Wireless network SSID: RUatHome
Important information for the RUatHome network
•	Each student has their own unique Passphrase (password) to add devices to the network. Do not share your password with others. 
•	In some instances, devices from the same brand, such as Apple or Android products, may automatically share wireless network passwords with your other devices, like a watch or tablet. Those devices may automatically connect to the network. You should check your connected devices and have them disconnect from the RUatHome network. 
•	The RUatHome network is only available to students in residence halls. It is not accessible by faculty/staff, and it is not available in other University buildings. 
o	The exception is faculty and staff living in On-Campus housing.
•	Some devices may require your phone to be on the same network as your device to complete the setup process or change device settings. In this case, you will have to add your phone to the RUatHome network as well. Phones should only be on the RUatHome network to assist with configuring your smart device. Once you are done configuring your device, you should promptly "Forget" the RUatHome network and connect to RUWireless Secure. This will ensure your phone maintains a wireless connection in all Rutgers buildings.  
Connecting your wireless devices
1.	Go to the Passphrase Portal. 
2.	Log in with your NetID and NetID password if you are not automatically logged in. 
3.	For devices with a camera, you can scan the QR code to automatically connect. 
4.	For other devices, note the password in the Passphrase field.  
o	These are valid for 1 year. You will automatically get an email as the expiration date approaches, prompting you to renew the key for an additional year. 

Error! Filename not specified.
5.	On your device, navigate to the wireless network settings. 
6.	Select the RUatHome network, which is only available in the residence halls. 
7.	Enter the Passphrase from step 4 as the network password. 
Disconnecting your wireless devices
•	To temporarily disconnect a device, you can power it off to ensure it no longer has an active wireless connection or go into the device's wireless network settings and choose to "Disconnect" from the network. 
•	To permanently disconnect a device, go into the device's wireless network settings and choose to "Forget" the network. You can always enter your Passphrase again if you want to reconnect it. 
Resetting your Passphrase 
You have the option to generate a new Passphrase. This should only be done in the rare event you need to, or are instructed to do so by the OIT Help Desk, as a step in troubleshooting any potential issues. 
1.	Go to the Passphrase Portal. 
2.	Log in with your NetID and NetID password if you are not automatically logged in. 
3.	Click on Generate New PassPhrase. 
4.	You'll receive a confirmation message that your current one will expire in 24 hours. Click Yes. 
5.	Your password will be updated and shown in the Passphrase field. 
6.	This also resets the expiration date of it to 359 days. 
7.	You will need to update any device using the old Passphrase. 
Devices still using the old Passphrase will remain connected for 24 hours after generating a new Passphrase.
Wired Devices 
For devices connecting to a Network port via an Ethernet cord, follow the instructions on connecting Wired devices to ResNet. 
Troubleshooting issues
•	The RUatHome network is only available in the residence halls. If you are not in a residence hall, you will not see RUatHome as a network you can join. 
•	RUatHome is only for use by active students, with the exception of faculty and staff living in On-Campus housing. If you do not fall into one of these categories, you will be unable to access the Passphrase portal. If you believe you qualify and can not access the portal, contact your local OIT Help Desk. 
•	Error messages:  
o	Incorrect Password for "RUatHome": Confirm that you entered your Passphrase correctly by logging into the Passphrase Portal and looking in the Passphrase field. 
•	For further assistance, contact your local IT Help Desk.

" KB0018798 ResNet Support Connecting Wired devices to ResNet "
To connect devices over WiFi in the residence hall, follow the instructions on how to connect your smart devices, streaming devices, and gaming consoles.
To connect a wired device through an Ethernet cord, follow the instructions below. 
For wired devices, you will have to submit a request to get your device connected. Please note that if you previously registered your device last year, you will not need to complete this form to reconnect it. Connecting via this method is only supported in the residence halls. 
Requirements
•	You must have an Ethernet cord connecting your device to the black or grey network port in your dorm/suite. If your device does not have an Ethernet port, you may purchase an adapter to use for a wired connection and use the MAC Address of the adapter when submitting your request.
•	Prior to submitting the form, ensure you have connected the device to the network port using an Ethernet cord and powered on your device.  
o	If requesting multiple devices, leave each device on and connected to the port for at least 30 seconds before connecting the next device.
•	Know the Wired MAC Address of your device. Note that a device that supports both wireless and wired network connections will have a different MAC Address for each. Ensure you use the wired MAC Address on the form. Otherwise, your request will not be processed, and you will experience a delay in establishing a Wired connection. 
•	If you need to connect multiple wired devices simultaneously and your residence lacks sufficient ports, you can use an Unmanaged Switch to expand the number of available ports. 
Submitting a request
1.	Find the Wired MAC Address of your device. 
2.	Log in to the Rutgers IT Help Portal and complete the EI - Wired ResNet Device Bypass form. 
3.	After submitting the form, your request will be reviewed. 
4.	You will receive an email once your request is processed, indicating whether or not your device was successfully added.  
o	Note: this is not an immediate process. 
5.	If it is a Windows device, you will need to disable the Wired Autoconfig service for it to connect properly.

" KB0013685 ResNet Support Getting your computer connected to ResNet in the residence halls "
The Rutgers University Office of Information Technology provides connections in residence halls. 
Students using computers in their rooms, connected to the Rutgers Network, must follow the ResNet Network rules regarding computer usage. If caught violating any of the rules, your connection may be terminated without warning.
How to connect to the network
Laptops should be set up to use RUWireless Secure. 
To gain access to the network with an Ethernet (wired) connection, follow the instructions on connecting your wired device. 
Configuring your operating system to obtain an IP automatically (DHCP)
Most devices will automatically use DHCP to obtain an IP address. If yours does not, follow the instructions below based on your operating system:
Windows
1.	Click on the Search Windows bar > search Control Panel. 
1.	At the top right where it says View by, if it says Category, change it to Small Icons or Large icons. This will show more options. 
2.	Click the Network and Sharing Center.
3.	Click the link for Local Area Connection.
4.	Click on Properties.
5.	Uncheck the box for Internet Protocol Version 6 (TCP/IPv6).
6.	Double-click on Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4).
7.	Select or check that the radio buttons for Obtain an IP address automatically and Obtain DNS server address automatically.
8.	Click OK to save the changes and close the window. Click OK to close the Properties window. Click Close in the Local Area Connection Status window.
MacOS
1.	From the Apple menu, select System Preferences. Select Network (Under Internet and Network). NOTE: Authentication may be required via the lock icon in the lower left corner.
2.	Select Ethernet on the left menu.
3.	Set Configure on the right screen to Using DHCP.
4.	Click the Apply Now button, then quit the System Preferences application.

" KB0013736 ResNet Support ResNet FAQ: Antivirus software and spyware "
My computer is infected with a virus. Why was my network connection shut off?
The OIT Acceptable Use Policy states that ResNet has the right to remove any machines deemed a threat from the network. Many viruses, "worms," and "Trojan horses" are designed to infect other computers they can find on the network. Computers identified as being infected with a virus will be disconnected from the network to protect others' computers from becoming infected. Please consider this as a protective measure and not as disciplinary action against you.
Where can I get anti-virus software?
Visit our Antivirus software page for more information. 
My computer is infected with a virus. What antivirus software should I use?
You can use any antivirus software you wish to keep your computer virus-free. Once your computer is disconnected due to a virus infection, you must either update your existing antivirus software or install the programs as recommended in the browsing best practices page above and eliminate the problem before your network connection is restored. You may also reimage or reformat your hard drive to remediate the problem.
Why does my web browser sometimes go to sites that I do not want it to go to?
You may have any of a variety of programs running invisibly. To remedy this situation, you must scan your computer for malicious software that may have been installed without your knowledge. We recommend programs like AdwCleaner and Malwarebytes to protect your machines from spyware.
Why does my internet/computer seem slower than usual?
Since spyware runs in the background of an operating system, it will still use some system resources. If a computer has enough spyware, there may be a noticeable slowdown in Internet speed, general computing speed, or both. Programs such as AdwCleaner or Malwarebytes can be used to help address this problem.
Why do I get popups when my computer is not attended?
Popups are most commonly seen when surfing the web but may also occur even when you are not at your computer. Pop-ups are typically caused by adware. Adware differs from spyware because adware is software that may have been installed on your computer by a remote site. Many free utilities that you download from the Internet will install hidden software that sends details of the websites you visit and other information from your computer (which can include your email address) to advertisers so they can target you with popup ads and spam. The easiest way to ensure your computer is clean from adware is to use AdwCleaner and Malwarebytes.
" KB0013735 ResNet Support ResNet network rules "
Students using computers in their rooms connected to the Rutgers Network must follow rules regarding computer usage. If caught violating any of the rules, your connection may be terminated without warning.
Rutgers Acceptable Use Policy for Computing and Information Technology Resources [PDF]
To ensure high-quality infrastructure for your academic purposes and consistent with the OIT Acceptable Use Policy, you must protect the access and integrity of your personal devices connected to the Rutgers Network, including but not limited to LANs behind personal routers and PCs running any operating system. The Office of Information Technology recommends that residents follow the best browsing practices outlined in the Antivirus section of the Rutgers IT website.
For more details regarding computer security, visit the Information Security site for tips and suggestions on how to keep your computer and information safe.
Below is a list of things NOT allowed on computers in the Residence Hall Network.
•	FTP servers containing copyrighted material (Software, MP3 Files, etc)
•	Excessive amounts of data, either inbound or outbound.
•	Web servers containing commercial content or used for commercial purposes.
•	Mail Servers: you cannot run a mail server on your computer.
•	Providing Network connections to ANYONE else. If your roommate wants a connection, they can get their own. It is perfectly OK to allow someone else to use your computer, you just cannot extend the Network to other people.
•	Ping attacks on other computers.
•	Servers and/or programs that end up using a lot of bandwidth.
•	Attempting to access computers on which you do not have accounts.
•	Registering your TCP/IP address with outside Domain Name Services.
•	Running ‘Bots’ (Robots) of any kind doing anything to other computers, especially IRC bots.
Router Use
Personal wireless routers are not allowed in Residence Halls. Unmanaged switches can be used in cases where you want numerous wired connections. Please contact the OIT Help Desk with any questions or if you believe your Residence Hall may not have full wireless coverage.
" KB0016540 ResNet Support ResNet Pop Up Help Desk for Move-In "
During Move-In, Pop Up Help Desk teams will be available in first-year student residence halls to facilitate a quick, efficient connection to the residence hall computer network. Most students will not experience difficulty with this process. However, should you experience problems, we strongly recommend that you speak with a Pop Up Help Desk representative while the teams are present in your residence hall. 
Please bring Ethernet cables to connect to the wired connection in your residence hall room and USB cables to connect to your printers. Wireless is available in all of the residence halls. Please visit kite+key, the Rutgers Tech Store, if you require any accessories.
The OIT Help Desk can also assist, but due to the large influx of students, expected phone wait times will be longer for the first several weeks of the semester. Please come to the nearest location to find a Pop Up team member.

" KB0013734 ResNet Support ResNet Wired & Wireless Setup "
Table of Contents
•	How do I get connected to the wired network?
•	Where can I purchase networking cables?
•	There are more residents assigned to my room than there are available Ethernet ports. How can everyone connect to the Internet?
•	Can I connect more than one device to the wired network in my room?
•	How do I set up my console gaming system on the network?
•	I got a new computer or device. What do I need to do to get connected?
•	Can I connect more than one device to the wireless network in my room?
•	Can I set up my printer in my room?
•	Can I set up my own wireless network or wireless access point in my residence hall?
•	Are there any devices that will not work on RUWireless Secure?
 
How do I get connected to the wired network?
Plug one end of your Ethernet cable into the Ethernet port on your computer. Plug the other end into the Ethernet jack in the wall. The jack is usually black, and the faceplate is labeled with a number and the letter "D". Follow the instructions on connecting Wired devices to ResNet. 
Where can I purchase networking cables?
Ethernet cables are available to Camden, Newark, and New Brunswick students at the kite+key Rutgers tech stores, and local electronics stores.
There are more residents assigned to my room than there are available Ethernet ports. How can everyone connect to the Internet?
In most cases, there is one Ethernet port available in each dorm/suite. You can obtain and use an Unmanaged Switch to connect multiple devices. 
Can I connect more than one device to the wired network in my room?
Although you can only connect one device per port to the wired network at a time, there is no restriction on the total number of network devices in a room. Residents who want to use more wired devices than there are ports would be required to disconnect the current device and then connect the new device to the same Ethernet port. You would still have to follow the instructions on connecting Wired devices to ResNet. 
If you need to have multiple wired devices connected simultaneously and you do not have enough ports in your residence, you may use an Unmanaged Switch to expand the number of available ports. 
Wireless routers are not permitted in residence halls, as they interfere with RUWireless.
How do I set up my console gaming system on the network?
If you wish to use a console on the network, you can connect wirelessly or through a wired connection. Follow the instructions on connecting your smart devices, streaming devices, gaming consoles, and desktops. 
I got a new computer or device. What do I need to do to get connected?
For laptops, phones, and tablets, please refer to the instructions on how to connect to RUWireless Secure. For all wired desktops and smart devices, follow the instructions on connecting your smart devices, streaming devices, gaming consoles, and desktops. 
Can I connect more than one device to the wireless network in my room?
There is no limit to the number of wireless devices you can connect to RUWireless Secure or RUatHome at a time.
Can I set up my printer in my room?
Wireless and wired capabilities of personal printers are not supported, but you can still connect with a USB cable to print.
Can I set up my own wireless network or wireless access point in my residence hall?
All Rutgers residence halls offer full RUWireless coverage. As a result, ResNet does not support the wireless feature for personal routers, as it interferes with the RUWireless signal for other residents. If you are unable to connect to RUWireless in your room due to poor coverage or believe RUWireless does not cover your residence hall, get in touch with your local OIT Help Desk for assistance.
Are there any devices that will not work on RUWireless Secure?
If your device does not support the RUWireless Secure installer, you may connect it to the RUatHome wireless network or configure it for a wired connection. These devices include wired desktops, game consoles, handheld game consoles, smart TVs, and smart assistants. Follow the instructions on connecting your smart devices, streaming devices, gaming consoles, and desktops.  
Please note that some devices may experience reduced functionality on the Rutgers wireless network compared to your home wireless network. Some wireless devices that support 2.4 GHz only may not be able to connect; it is recommended to use a wireless device capable of 5 GHz. 
Additionally, some devices are not supported on our residential wireless networks in any capacity. These devices include:
•	Google Chromecast
•	Certain Smart Plugs & Lights
•	Network Printers
" KB0013684 ResNet Support ResNet wired setup – 180 West Market Street "
How do I get connected to the wired network?
Follow the instructions in the wired section of the article on connecting Wired devices to ResNet.
Can I connect more than one device to the wired network in my room?
Although you can only connect one device per port to the wired network at a time, you can use an Unmanaged Switch to increase the number of ports available to you. Residents with more wired devices than there are ports may disconnect the current device and then connect the new device to the same Ethernet port.
How do I set up my console gaming system on the network?
If you wish to use a console on the network, follow the instructions on connecting your smart devices, streaming devices, gaming consoles, and desktops.
I got a new computer or device. What do I need to do to get connected?

Can I use a personal router in my apartment?

" KB0014534 ResNet Support TV service at Rutgers "
Rutgers is making significant updates to the television services provided on campus. In response to the evolving media landscape and your changing viewing habits, we have phased out traditional cable television service. This change will affect both residential areas, including rooms and apartments, as well as public spaces throughout the university. 
Traditional cable television service is discontinued in all on-campus residence hall rooms, apartments, and community lounge spaces. This decision comes as a direct response to your preferences and habits. 
Your feedback over the years has informed a significant shift towards online streaming content. Platforms like YouTube, Netflix, and others are not just your choices, they are part of your daily life. These streaming services offer more flexibility and variety, over traditional cable connections. This trend is evident in the increased use of our campus Wi-Fi system for accessing content, signaling a departure from coaxial cable. 
It’s important to us that all our students enjoy a wide range of media content without financial barriers. To this end, we put together a comprehensive guide to various streaming services that offer either free content or attractive student discounts. 
These options are tailored for use on personal devices within our residential buildings, ensuring that you can easily access your favorite shows and movies right from your dorm room or apartment. To make use of these plans, all you need is to show proof of your current enrollment at Rutgers. 
Learn more about the available streaming plans and how to take advantage of these student discounts.

Migrating your workstation to the RAD domain
Before you begin, you must understand and verify the following:
•	The workstation OS must be at least Windows 7 or higher.
•	Enterprise KACE will be installed on each workstation via Group Policy.
o	KACE can be managed by your Admins or KACE can be managed by OIT.
•	Have the Local Administrator account of your workstation on hand.
o	This is required when you unjoin your workstation in the steps below.
•	The PC object must exist in the correct OU before migrating the PC, and the PC name must match the PC name in AD.
•	The -adm account that creates the PC object needs to join the PC object to RAD
1.	Click on Start > Control Panel > System and Security > System.
2.	On the right-hand side under "Computer name, domains and workgroup settings," click on Change Settings.

Error! Filename not specified.
3.	In System Properties, click Change… and change the computer name to the RAD-specified computer name and add the computer to the workgroup.
4.	Reboot and log in as the local admin account.
5.	Repeat Steps 3 and 4.
6.	Click Change and add the workstation to RAD.RUTGERS.EDU.
7.	Reboot and log in with your RAD account.
8.	Confirm that DNS is pointing to 128.6.1.1.

" KB0014512 Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) Azure Hybrid Join configuration profile "
Hybrid Azure AD Join has been implemented with Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) and is available for use. A device is said to be hybrid joined if it has both an AD object and an Azure AD (AAD) object, which allows users of that device to sign in with a RAD user account.
With Hybrid Joins the university can now leverage:
•	Device Based licensing for Office 365
o	This allows Office to be tied to the Device rather than the User, making it ideal for enterprise or shared devices.
•	Reduced logins due to the device being assign both RAD and Azure authentication tokens
A device in Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) can end up in a hybrid joined state one of two ways:
•	If the computer is already joined to RAD.
•	The computer was built using Rutgers Autopilot, which allows for hybrid-joining via configuration profiles.
A hybrid joined computer is joined to both AD and AAD, but the AD join is primary because the device initially uses AD authentication. Only Windows devices can be hybrid joined.
Azure Hybrid Join Configuration Profile
AD Join from Azure Configuration Profile. NOTE: This is NOT required if the device is already part of RAD. It is only required for new deployments or Azure Only Joined devices.
1.	Log in to Microsoft Endpoint, then click on Devices. Under the Policy heading, click Configuration Profiles.

Error! Filename not specified.
2.	Click Create Profile, select Windows 10 and Later as the Platform and Templates as the Type.


Error! Filename not specified.
3.	Find Domain Join in the list and click Create.

Error! Filename not specified.
4.	Name your Configuration and click Next.

Error! Filename not specified. 
5.	Here we will specify the prefix for the system, domain, and OU for it to be placed in.
1.	The Computer Name Prefix can be 12 characters long, allowing Azure to randomly assign the last 3 characters to be unique. This prevents us from pre-populating computer names in RAD.
2.	Enter the Domain you wish to join.
3.	Add the FQDN of the OU where you wish for the devices to be added.
4.	Click Next.

Error! Filename not specified.
6.	You will then need to set the Scope Tag for your department and assign the Configuration to a group of devices for assignment.
7.	The Intune Connector will create the Computer Object and join the device on your behalf.
8.	Devices that are decommissioned or re-imaged will need to be reset and manually removed from AD.
" KB0014470 Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) Connecting to AD via LDAP in Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) "
Request a Service account to bind LDAP to AD:
To submit a request, fill out the Request Service and Generic Accounts form. Select the appropriate account, follow the instructions to complete the fields, and then submit.
RAD LDAP Info
We have worked with the EI network team to create two Virtual IPs (VIPs) for Rad LDAP. This will ensure failover in the event that any DCs are offline, and fault isolation in the case of an outage at one of the EI Data centers. These VIP’s need to use a secure connection on port 636. If using RAD for LDAP, please update your settings to use the info below.
The server names are:
•	Primary = rad-ldap.rutgers.edu
•	Secondary = rad-ldap2.rutgers.edu
The Base DN is:
•	DC=rad
•	DC=Rutgers
•	DC=edu
The ports to bind is Secure Port: 636.

" KB0014481 Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) How do I access Isilon Storage from Home? "
Follow the instructions below when trying to access Isilon Storage outside of the Rutgers University campus:
1.	Connect to the Rutgers VPN.
2.	Use Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) to connect to your office desktop and access the mapped Shared Drives.
If RDP is not available, you can access RAD Shares remotely. After connecting to the appropriate VPN, you can access RAD Shares, which are housed on Isilon Storage.
•	If on RAD-bound machines, you should be able to connect by DFS link. Please contact your local IT Support to determine which DFS link you should use to access your RAD storage.
o	Example DFS Link: \\rad.rutgers.edu\dfs\RADHomeShares
•	If on Stand Alone non-Managed machines, you should be able to access the storage by SMB Path. Contact your local IT Support to determine which SMB Path you should use to access your RAD storage.
o	Example SMB Path: \\isilon-1-asb-smb.ei.rutgers.edu\home
If data is stored on OneDrive or Box, you won't need to connect to the VPN to access it.

" KB0014471 Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) How to get started with RAD (Rutgers Active Directory) "
Management of your AD environment is done through delegated Organizational Units (OU) in RAD. To manage your AD environment, a request from IT Leadership within your organization is required. Delegated OUs provide a secure Windows domain environment. Delegated OUs will enable RU to remove Windows domain silos, share resources, and reduce costs, making it easier to share resources.
Requesting Delegated Organizational Units
Requests for a delegated OU can be made from the IT Leadership in your organization by submitting the RAD Data Collection form. In the request, ensure that you include the technical contacts, the department head, and the suggested OU name. Delegated OU names should be short; we will typically recommend using the Departmental Code as assigned in Cornerstone. (i.e., OIT, ORA, SAS)
It can take between a couple of days to a couple of months to join, depending on the complexity of your existing environment. " KB0014497 Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) Managing your Delegated OU in RAD "
Designated department IT staff will use a non-standard NetID account in RAD with elevated rights to perform the functions below. These are known as ADM accounts. Learn more on how to get access to Rad ADM accounts. Once created, these accounts would be added to the Departmental-OU admins or Departmental-Workstations admins group, depending on the level of access required.
OIT has defined naming convention guidelines for RAD objects. When creating these objects, OIT requires that you prefix the object with your delegated OU name if our naming standards do not meet your requirements.
Delegated -OU Admins will have full rights to manage their OU’s, as described below, except for manipulating standard NetID accounts. These accounts all reside in the People OU, which is managed by IDM, and any changes should originate from IDM processes. Passwords should be managed through netid.rutgers.edu to ensure all accounts stay in Sync (Portal, Luminous, AD, Email).
Create and edit group policies
OIT will create a Workstation baseline GP at the root of your delegated OU to enforce Loopback Group Policy-Merge and populate the Built-in Administrator’s group of each managed workstation with the departmental Workstation Admins group.
•	Group Policy Loopback Processing needs to be set to ‘Merge’. Since all user accounts are located in the People OU, we need to instruct the PC Objects to process the user policies assigned to the machine. This allows user configurations to run on machines when the user isn’t in the same OU. This only needs to be set once on a machine, and other delegated areas will set it in their workstation baseline policy.
•	Share mappings can be configured on this GP, and it can also be used to push PC settings down to all Workstations within the delegated OU.
•	Additional information can be found on the Microsoft site: Loopback processing of Group Policy.
Security groups
OIT will create these default groups when setting up your delegated OU. All other groups will be created by the delegated OU administrators.
•	OU-OU Admins
•	OU-Workstations Admins
•	OU-All Users
•	OU-All Workstations
•	OU-Restricted
Important notes regarding OU Admins vs Workstations Admin Group
Non-ADM accounts should NOT be members of the OU Admins or OU Workstation Admin groups.
ADM accounts should only be in one group or the other. Being in the OU Admins group can grant technicians more access than they need. OU Admins are already nested members of the Workstation Admin groups. If they only need Workstation Admin rights, they would be in the Workstation Admin group only. 
OU Admins: Users in this group are recommended to have the following permissions and responsibilities:
•	The permissions to modify rights over Groups, OUs, Group Policies, and Printers.
•	Creating and assigning group policies to control settings for the users and computers within the delegated OU.
•	Delegating certain administrative tasks to other users or groups within the delegated OU.
•	OU Admins are already members of the Delegated OU-Workstation Admins group.
Workstations Admins: Users in this group are recommended to have the following permissions and responsibilities:
•	The rights to migrate workstations to the domain, administrative rights over delegated OU workstations, and can add machines to the Delegated OU-All Workstations group.
•	Installing, configuring, and updating software applications on workstations.
•	Managing hardware configurations and drivers on individual computers.
•	Troubleshooting and resolving issues related to specific workstations.
•	Ensuring that workstations are compliant with security policies and updates.
•	Providing user support for workstation-related problems.
Organization Units (OUs)
Each OU admin will have the ability to create and delete Sub-OUs within their Delegated OU.
Printer objects
Listed in the directory and able to be set up as print queues or mapped by direct IP printing. Print Management is performed through an MMC snap-in, which is configured to connect to the print server hosting your print queue.
You can request that print queues be created on the Enterprise RAD print server (ASBRADPRINT01, 172.29.219.151) using this form. 
•	Please ensure the Request Category: RAD-Rutgers Active Directory, and the Request Type = Printers. We need the following info to set up a print queue.
•	Print queue name: Must begin with Delegated OU name.
•	IP: Please ensure that you can access our print server from your subnet.
•	Driver to user: link to the driver you want us to use for this print queue.
Shared drives
Managing Restricted Drive NTFS Permissions: Only applies to schools that have requested Enterprise On-premises storage.
•	Each School’s OU admin group will be given 'Modify' rights over the storage allocated to their school.
•	Each School will have a Global Restricted (R) drive.
o	User would have to be added to the top-level Restricted group to have the drive mapped (OU-Restricted)
o	For each folder within this Drive, there should also be a corresponding AD security group created and added to the security of the folder
o	Access Based Enumeration (ABE) is enabled on Enterprise storage Servers, ensuring users will only be able to view folders they have permission to access
o	User would need to be a member of the following groups
	OU-All Users
	OU-Restricted
	OU-Restricted (Name of Folder)
•	Each school will have a Shared (S) drive mapped.
o	The department drive is designed to be accessible to anyone within the department.
o	‘Modify’ permissions are automatically granted to anyone who is a member of the ‘OU-All Users’ group within the department’s Organizational Unit (OU).
•	Each school must request Home Drive space, which is a separate location from Departmental shares
o	Their H Drive (Home): Personal server storage location for saving work-related files.
o	Restricted to the individual user and could potentially mitigate data loss if stored on the network instead of locally.
Delegated OU-Workstation Admins will have rights to migrate machines to RAD and have administrative rights over the Departmental workstations through the Departmental Workstation baseline Group Policy. Delegated OU admins are members of the Workstation Admins group by default and have the same rights over PC objects as described below.
PC objects
All machines to be migrated will have to be pre-created in the Delegated OU before they can be migrated. OIT has defined standard naming convention to be used for RAD managed PC objects.
PC management should be done through ADUC (Active Directory Users and Computers), or ADAC (Active Directory Administrative Center).
Once added to the delegated OU’s All workstations group, the baseline policy will allow them to have administrative access over these devices.
This group is also granted 'Modify' rights over their departmental print queues.
