" KB0012478 Rutgers Connect Common use cases for SharePoint "
The right collaboration environment is crucial for department performance, engagement, and innovation. SharePoint’s versatility allows the service to be utilized for a large variety of objectives ranging from basic information storage to complex project dashboards.
Table of Contents
•	Content Management
•	Intranets
•	Business process Automation/Workflow Management
•	Project Management
Content Management
SharePoint allows users to create, edit, submit, approve and publish 2.5 TB worth of content for a given site collection or group. This content can be shared and made viewable to specified users. Using built-in document libraries and lists, users can organize where they store their content within a site. Content can consist of a variety of types (text, video, graphics, audio). The most important content management capabilities of SharePoint include:
•	Versioning
•	Real-time collaboration
•	Approvals
•	Indexing
•	Search
Intranets
SharePoint excels as an intranet platform as it offers a wide variety of out-of-the-box functionalities. These capabilities let users design an effective intranet for their department with ease. These features consist of:
•	Branded home page
•	Multi-functional web parts that integrate with various Microsoft services
•	Custom navigation
•	Flexible content sharing options
•	Modern/classic team and communication sites
•	Social features (communities, forums, media galleries)
•	Mobile access
Error! Filename not specified.
Business process Automation/Workflow Management
SharePoint supports business process management as it offers a variety of options for implementing, maintaining, and executing workflows. Many common workflow processes come built-in to the service such as getting approvals, collecting feedback, and acquiring signatures. Furthermore, SharePoint integrates with a variety of Office 365 tools (Word, OneNote, OneDrive) which facilitates the creation of content-related workflows. Users can create custom workflows through SharePoint’s integration with Power Automate (formerly Microsoft Flow).
Project Management
SharePoint is a popular and practical solution for project management, as it allows a project’s information to be stored in a central place. Using the out-of-the-box project management features, SharePoint holds the capabilities for successful project visibility, reporting, collaboration, and delivery. A SharePoint site acts as home for a user's project information and content. A SharePoint site collection collects multiple projects into a project portfolio. Within these sites, SharePoint lists help organize project information while web parts make reporting easy. Additionally, users can use the built-in project site template or integrate Microsoft Project for their project management needs.

" KB0017401 Rutgers Connect Creating and updating Email signatures in Connect "
Creating or updating your signature
To create your email signature on Rutgers Connect, follow the instructions below. You may also create and update your signature on both the Classic and New versions of Outlook for Windows or Outlook for Mac. 
1.	Log in to Rutgers Connect and click the gear icon at the top right-hand side.
2.	Navigate to Mail > Compose and Reply > Email Signature.
3.	Create your signature using these recommendations: 
o	Type and format your signature inside the Outlook signature window. Creating your signature in an outside program (like Word) and copying into the window may cause formatting issues. 
o	Use a common font such as Calibri or Times New Roman. Other fonts may not display correctly.
o	Use a single font color such as black or gray.
o	Example signature format: 
	First Name Last Name (pronouns optional)
Job title
Department/group/unit
Specific campus and/or Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey
Preferred contact phone number
Office address (optional)
Website/social media links (optional)

1.	Click in your signature where you want the logotype to appear.
2.	Click on the Insert Image icon in the toolbar.
3.	Navigate to the file you want to use, as described in the next section, and click Open. 
4.	Resize the image as needed. 
5.	Click Save. 
Getting the Rutgers logotype for use in your signature
Using the standard Rutgers University logotype
1.	Go to the Email Signatures section of the Rutgers University Stationery and Templates page. 
2.	Select the desired logotype format.
3.	This will bring you to a SharePoint page where you can download the .SVG file to be used in your email signature. The all Red option is best for both light and dark mode on devices. The Red and Black option is most visible in light mode on devices. 
Using your departmental specific logotype
If your department has a specific logotype (ex: Office of Information Technology, Mason Gross School of the Arts, New Jersey Medical School, Office for Research, etc.) you have to first obtain it from the Rutgers University Signature Generator. Note that the Signature Generator does not create a signature for you; it only provides the logotype file to be used in your signature. It's recommended to use the .SVG file type for an email signature. 
1.	Log in to the Rutgers University Signature Generator.
2.	Click Search to look through the existing approved logotypes. 
3.	Locate the department you are in and click Download Package.  
o	Any packages that are labeled "(vertical R)" do not contain the email signature logotype. Download a package not labeled as vertical instead. 
o	If your department is not listed, you may return to the previous page and click Request to fill out the form requesting a logotype be created for your department. 
4.	Open the .zip file that was downloaded. 
5.	Open the E-SIGNATURE folder and use the .svg file.

" KB0012504 Rutgers Connect Email encryption for Rutgers Connect "
Under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA), all communications containing Protected Health Information (PHI) must be encrypted. To ensure the confidentiality of private information sent via email and comply with HIPAA privacy regulations, Rutgers Connect uses multiple approaches to keep your information safe.
All email sent by users with PHI flags is automatically protected with TLS Secure email. TLS is a cryptographic protocol that provides security between email servers. Most email servers are configured to receive email sent via TLS. Rutgers is aware of some common email servers that are not equipped for TLS. If a PHI-flagged person sends an email to one of these known email servers, Rutgers Connect will automatically use the built-in capabilities of Office 365's Office Message Encryption (OME) to protect your email.
If a PHI-flagged person attempts to send an email to an email server that does not support TLS and is not known to Rutgers Connect, the sender will receive a bounce-back. Please review the following article to learn more about what to expect if you encounter this issue.
Please note: For backward compatibility with our previous encryption service, Zix Corporation, any message containing the keyword “ZIXSECURE” in the subject or body and leaving Rutgers Connect will have OME encryption applied. OIT does not recommend using keywords to force encryption. The keyword feature has been retained for specialized cases and may be removed completely in the future, as it is being replaced by OME's encryption features.
Secure messaging is not just a government mandate; it is a practical way to conduct business. Email is not a private conversation; unencrypted email messages can be intercepted and read. Users can also protect emails that do not contain Protected Health Information by using the options provided by Office Message Encryption (OME).
The following documentation pages explain how Office Message Encryption (OME) works.
•	Recipient Experience
•	Sending Encrypted Email

This eventually leads the device to be marked as non-compliant, and causes Email, Teams, OneDrive, and other apps to stop working. " KB0019416 Rutgers Connect Exporting Publisher files "
Microsoft has announced permanent retirement for Microsoft Publisher on October 1, 2026. After that date, Publisher will no longer be included in Microsoft 365 subscriptions, and support for existing versions will end. 
Considering this, it's recommend to convert your existing files to another format before the October 1, 2026 support cutoff. After this date, you will no longer be able to open or edit these files in Microsoft Publisher.  
Details
After October 1, 2026:
•	Publisher will be removed from Microsoft 365 installations.
•	Microsoft 365 subscribers will no longer be able to open or edit Publisher (.pub) files in the application.
Versions include:
•	Publisher for Microsoft 365
•	Publisher 2021 (see note)
•	Publisher 2019 (see note)
•	Publisher 2016
•	Publisher 2013
•	Publisher 2010
Note: Standalone versions (e.g.: "Publisher 2019", "Publisher 2021") may continue to function but will no longer receive updates or security fixes from Microsoft.
Exporting and Modifying Publisher files
Converting Publisher files to PDF (for viewing) 
To view content after Publishers retirement, you can convert the file to a PDF format by:
1.	Open Publisher file.
2.	Go to File > Save as.
3.	Choose a location to save the file.
4.	Select PDF as the file type and Save.
Converting numerous Publisher files
It is highly recommended that you have an IT representative assist you with this method. For assistance in finding or contacting your departmental IT or the OIT Help Desk.
To convert many Publisher files, consider automating this process by using a PowerShell script. You can refer to Example conversion script (located as a dropdown option below the paragraph on the linked site) as a guide.
Converting Publisher files to Word (for editing)
To edit content after Publishers retirement, you can convert the file through Word or through a third-party conversion tool (noted in Alternate option section).
For Word:
1.	Open Word.
2.	Go to File > Open.
3.	Locate and open the PDF file.
4.	Select OK in the dialog box.
From here your document will open as a Word file.
Note: The converted Word document will be optimized for text editing. As a result, its layout may vary from the original PDF—particularly if the document includes many graphics.
Alternate option to convert Publisher files
Using a third-party conversion tool to convert directly from Publisher to another file type.
Note: These services vary in quality and capabilities, and Microsoft does not provide support for them.

" KB0012525 Rutgers Connect Getting started with Microsoft Teams "
Set up Microsoft Teams
Microsoft Teams is available as a download for a desktop app and as a mobile app for iOS and Android.
You can also run Microsoft Teams through the Teams website.
Sign in to Microsoft Teams
Logging in via the web app
1.	Go to Rutgers Connect. 
2.	The login name should be entered as netid@domain.rutgers.edu.
3.	Enter your NetID password > Sign In.
4.	Select the Waffle icon located in the upper left corner.
5.	From the drop-down menu, select Teams.
Logging in via the desktop app
After downloading the application, you will be asked to sign in with your work or school account.
1.	The login name should be entered as netid@domain.rutgers.edu
2.	Enter your NetID password > Sign In.

     Error! Filename not specified.
Select a Team and Channel
A team is a collection of people, conversations, files, and tools — all in one place. A channel is a discussion topic in a team. The best way to get familiar with teams and channels is to select a team and channel and start exploring. If you're not on a Team and want to create one, please talk to your domain admin.
1.	Select the Teams icon.

     Error! Filename not specified.
2.	Select a channel and explore the Conversations, Files, and Notes tabs.
Channels can be a department, project, or topic. For more info, see Teams and channels.
Getting to Know the Microsoft Teams Layout
When you open Microsoft Teams, the name of the current view is centered at the top of the screen. Microsoft Teams usually opens to the last view you used. A vertical toolbar resides on the left side of the screen. Its upper left corner contains buttons for the main views: Activity, Chat, Teams, Meetings, and Files. Some buttons may not be available, depending on your account type. In the lower left corner of the toolbar are the buttons for Feedback and Settings (your icon). Notification settings are synced with the server; changes made in the browser will be reflected in the desktop client.
The rest of the screen is divided into two panes. Pane content depends on the current view. The left or list pane is used to navigate within the view. It always contains the Search field. The rest of its contents depend on the selected view. For example, if you select Chat on the toolbar, the left pane contains a list of your favorite, recent, and suggested contacts.
The right or main pane takes up most of the screen. It shows the content of the selection you have made in the left pane. For example, if you selected Chat on the toolbar and then selected a recent contact in the left pane, the right pane contains your conversation history with that person. The right pane also has tabs to keep the content organized. For example, in Chat view, the Conversation tab contains the conversation history, the Files tab contains a list of the files shared between you and the selected contact, the Organization tab shows the position of the selected contact in the organization chart, and so on.

" KB0012549 Rutgers Connect How to create an automatic reply message in Rutgers Connect "
1.	When logged into Rutgers Connect, click on the gear icon in the upper right corner to open Settings.
2.	Select View all Outlook settings at the bottom of the tab. 
3.	Choose Mail > Automatic replies.
4.	Toggle on the Turn on automatic replies option. 
o	You have the option to either set your reply to start at a specific time, or to continue until you turn it off manually. 
	To set your reply to start at a specific time, check the Send replies only during this time period checkbox, then select a start time and an end time.
	To set your reply to continue until you turn it off manually, leave this option unchecked.
5.	Type your reply in the Send automatic replies inside your organization window.
6.	You have the option to send a separate reply to correspondents outside of Rutgers Connect. 
o	To use this, check the Send replies outside your organization checkbox.
o	You can choose to send replies to all senders or to those senders whose addresses are found in your contact list only by selecting the Send replies only to contacts checkbox.
o	If you wish to send the same reply to all external senders, copy your reply from the message window above and paste it into the Send replies outside your organization section.
o	Otherwise, enter a new message for your external senders in this section.
7.	Scroll to the bottom of the window and click Save.
8.	If you wish to turn off automatic replies manually, return to this page as described above, and toggle off the Automatic replies option.
9.	Scroll to the bottom of the window and click Save.

Outlook Web Access (OWA) Login

     Error! Filename not specified.
3.	In the Share with field, enter the name or email of the user you want to share the calendar with, then select them from the results menu below the search field. 

     Error! Filename not specified.
4.	For each user you add, select the level of access they should have for the calendar.

     Error! Filename not specified.
o	Availability only means they will only see events as free or busy, and cannot see subjects or details.
o	Limited details means they will be able to see the subjects of events, but cannot see details.
o	Full details means they will see subjects and details for events.
o	Editor means they can also add or edit events.
o	Delegate means they will receive copies of all events for the calendar in their personal inbox and can accept/decline events on behalf of the calendar.

     Error! Filename not specified.

" KB0015504 Rutgers Connect Manage your Connect Devices and Licenses "
With the number of devices now used for work, it can be confusing to figure out which site you need to go to to troubleshoot issues you might be facing. The following guide is intended to help you reach the correct device management page for Connect-related services.
•	Personal Device Registrations – These are devices you may have registered through the Intune Company Portal app to access your email or other services offered by Rutgers. In most cases, these are cell phones, but if you registered a tablet, it would fall under this category as well.
•	Office Activations – Your Office license includes 5 activations you can use on any devices you want. The devices that will show on this list are the ones you’ve signed into Office with your Connect credentials.
•	Accidental Device Registrations – These often come up during an Office activation.
Personal Device Registrations
Registering your device through the Intune Company Portal app allows you to access various Rutgers-approved apps for work use and, most importantly, provides access to your email and calendar on the go.
You can have up to 20 devices registered, with no more than 5 per OS (iOS, iPadOS, Android, Android for Work, Windows). It is recommended to remove device registrations when you no longer use those devices. You can manage your Intune-registered devices in two locations:
•	Via the Microsoft Device Portal.
o	This will take you to a landing page where you will see any device currently registered through the Intune Company Portal app. You can click on each one to see more details. More information on all the available options on this page can be found on Microsoft’s self-service guide.
•	Through the Intune Company Portal app on your registered device
o	By launching the app, you will see a list of your registered devices by default, where you can tap any device to see more details.
If you need to add a new device or remove an old one, please review the guides on enabling mobile device management on Android or iOS, which will walk you through the entire process from start to finish.
Office Activations
You may see an error that you cannot use Microsoft apps after signing in to Office, and receive an alert that it’s running in “reduced functionality” mode. This usually means that you have too many Office activations, and it isn’t necessarily a problem with your device itself. While Microsoft says it will automatically deactivate the oldest registered device, it is best to verify this by visiting the Get Office webpage.
Once it loads, you should see a Devices dropdown menu where you will then be presented with all the devices you are currently signed into Office with that are using an activation.
Error! Filename not specified.
To free up activations for whatever new device you’re trying to register with, click the Sign out button on any extra devices you know you aren’t using Office apps on. Once you’re under the limit, you should be able to use the Office apps installed on the new device.
Accidental Registrations
At some point, you may have accidentally registered a personal computer with Rutgers without even realizing it. While it might not be immediately noticeable, accidentally linking your work account to your personal computer can have unintended consequences that may interrupt your use of the machine. Make sure to follow this guide through to completion prior to your Faculty, Staff, Student, or Guest role with Rutgers ends. Otherwise, you might be left needing to completely format your Windows PC if you wait until after you’ve left the university, retired, or become an Alumni.
When installing or logging into Office on a new machine, you will be prompted with the following:
Error! Filename not specified.
You always want to select No, this app only. In the event you left the Allow my organization to manage my device box checked and clicked OK, you will need to remove your work account from your machine by doing the following:
1.	Open the settings on your device and select Accounts.

Error! Filename not specified.
2.	Select the Access work or school section on the left-hand side, and check to see if your Connect account is displayed on this page, like in the image below.

Error! Filename not specified.

" KB0012615 Rutgers Connect Microsoft 365 groups "
Microsoft 365 Groups is a collaborative feature within Rutgers Connect that enables users to access shared versions of the following:
A Microsoft 365 group lets you choose a set of people you want to collaborate with and easily set up a collection of resources for them to share. Items in the group's resources (Calendar, OneDrive, OneNote) will automatically be shared with the group's members.
For additional information, visit the Microsoft page on adding/removing Group members.
Microsoft 365 groups within Rutgers Connect currently offer the following resources.
Shared inbox
Each group has a shared inbox accessible to all members. This shared inbox is fully searchable, creating a living archive of the group's messages. Newcomers to the group can search or scroll through the history to quickly get up to speed on what's been posted.
Messages addressed to the group's common email address will be delivered to this inbox. Members of the group can elect to have group messages appear in their personal inbox by subscribing to the group via email.
For additional information, visit the Microsoft page for Office 365's Shared Email.
Shared files library
Your group has a SharePoint file library where your users can store, share, and collaborate on documents, workbooks, presentations, images, or any other kind of file they need to work on.
Files stored in the group's file library can be edited using Microsoft Office desktop products as well as Office Online (Word Online, Excel Online, PowerPoint Online, etc.). These files have version control, which will track all changes made and also allow recovery to previous versions. Group libraries can also be shared with users external to the group.
For additional information, visit the Microsoft page for Office 365's Shared files library.
Shared calendar
Each group owns a shared calendar to post events related to the group. Each member who has subscribed to the group is automatically invited to events posted to the calendar, so those events can also appear on their personal calendars if they wish.
Group calendars can be shared with users external to the group.
For additional information, visit the Microsoft page for Office 365's Shared Calendar.
Shared OneNote Notebook
The group automatically has a shared OneNote notebook where group members can collect and collaborate on information.
•	
o	OneNote allows information to be organized in multiple tiers – notebooks, sections, pages, and subpages – which makes it easy to peruse only the relevant documentation. It also offers highly capable search functionality; users can search across all the information they have access to, or search only in a single page, section, or notebook. Additionally, it allows embedding a wide variety of media types, including images, audio recordings, and videos, to provide a more immersive and in-depth information-gathering experience.
o	Another common application is creating and storing meeting notes. As mentioned, OneNote allows users to embed audio recordings, and it also lets users record audio within OneNote. Recording can start at the beginning of the meeting without preventing any further note-taking; the person responsible for meeting notes can continue taking notes for the duration of the recording. Furthermore, any notes taken during this time will be associated with the appropriate time in the recording. If there is a brief note about a topic of interest, the note can be clicked on at a later time, and the recording will jump to the point at which that note was taken, so there is no need to sift through a long recording to find the bit of information you want.
o	Another feature of OneNote is handwriting recognition, so those who are more comfortable taking notes by hand can do so on a tablet or touchscreen-enabled computer, and their handwriting will be automatically converted to typed text.
Although there are many other uses for OneNote, the last one mentioned here is brainstorming. As the notebook is shared with all group members and can be updated in real time, colleagues can collaborate remotely by typing and drawing on a virtual paper that everyone can see at once.
To access OneNote, select the Notebook located on the top navigation bar in the group's view.

     Error! Filename not specified.
Guest access
You could add external contacts to distribution groups before, but all they got was email. With groups, you can offer guests access to email conversations, files, and even the shared OneNote notebook.
For additional information, visit the Microsoft page on Guest access.
If you would like to request the creation of an Office 365 group, please contact your Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator.
" KB0012604 Rutgers Connect Microsoft Bookings "
Microsoft Bookings is a scheduling tool that assists with booking appointments, and it is included with your Rutgers Connect Office 365 license. There are many ways to use Bookings in a university environment. An individual faculty member could use it to create a calendar where students could request office hour appointments, or a department chair or administrator could create an office hours calendar with slots for multiple faculty members.
You should be able to see the Bookings tab listed in the application menu after logging in to Rutgers Connect. Before you can access Bookings, however, you must either create a new Booking Calendar or be added to an existing Booking Calendar.
A Booking Calendar is a space where scheduling appointments can be made. Please note that currently, you are not able to create a Booking Calendar yourself through the Bookings application. You can contact your department or unit IT support to set up your Booking site to begin scheduling appointments. Once your Booking Calendar has been created by your department or unit IT support and you have been made an owner, you should be able to open the Bookings tab via your Rutgers Connect account and immediately access the site.
You can learn more about Bookings in this article from Microsoft, which goes into greater detail about the product.
     Error! Filename not specified.

•	Scheduling
•	Calendar
•	Booking Page
•	Staff
•	Services
•	Business Information
•	Additional Information
Scheduling
Bookings can be scheduled by either a user looking to make an appointment or a staff member with access to the Booking calendar. You can set up a booking page that allows users to schedule their own appointments, similar to what you might see if you have booked an appointment online to get a haircut or have your car serviced. Alternatively, you or another faculty or staff member can enter the bookings manually, such as when a user or customer calls for an appointment.
Calendar
The Calendar section lets you manually create and assign new Booking slots to users and staff members. It’s also where you can view all slots in your Bookings Calendar.
In order to manually set up and assign Booking slots, you will first need to create an entry for the customer in the “Customers” Booking tab. This will allow you to schedule appointments on behalf of users by inputting their contact information and details – the same details a user would need to provide if they were scheduling themselves for a Bookings slot. Next, navigate to the “Calendar” tab. Here you will be able to assign a Booking to both a customer and a staff member for a specific slot. This is a great feature for those who wish to keep their calendar hidden and keep track of appointments themselves within the app.
Booking Page
The Booking Page tab lets you make changes to and publish or unpublish the Booking Calendar. It also provides you with notification and scheduling settings that you can configure for your calendar. Here is what a published Bookings site looks like, where users can assign themselves to slots on a calendar when specified. 
     Error! Filename not specified.
Staff
Staff members are the employees that the users or customers book appointments with. If, for example, you were making a Bookings Calendar for an academic department office hours, these would be the department faculty. To add staff members to your Bookings Calendar, navigate to the Staff page and select Add Staff Member. This will bring up details you can edit for each member you wish to add. You can edit a staff member’s availability, contact information, and role: Administrator, Viewer or Guest.
Staff members can then be assigned to a variety of slots based on the availability presented on their Rutgers Connect calendar.
Administrators	Can open and configure the Booking Calendar. If we use the example of a department using bookings for faculty office hours, this might be the department chair or the administrative assistant. It could also be the faculty members if they want to manage their own booking calendar.
Viewers	Can open the Booking Calendar and view settings, but can’t make changes. If we use the example of a department using bookings for faculty office hours, this might be a student worker who you want to be able to view, but not change, appointments.
Guest	Can be assigned to a Booking slot, but cannot open the Booking Calendar. If we use the example of a department using bookings for faculty office hours, this might be a faculty member who is not managing the entire Booking calendar.
Customers	Are users who are booking the slots in the Calendar with a staff member. If we use the example of a department using bookings for faculty office hours, this might be the students booking office hours appointments.
 
     Error! Filename not specified.
Services
The Service tab is where you can edit the name of the service you are providing through your Booking Calendar. This is what customers see when a Booking Calendar is published – it should define the purpose of the Booking. If we use the example of a department using bookings for faculty office hours, this might be "Office Hours."
Business Information
The Business Information tab lets you configure the overall name of your calendar as well as the business/office hours, contact information and logo so that customers can easily identify the group associated with the service.
The slots that are created in the calendar are unique to the Booking Calendar itself.
Additional Information
You can find more advanced documentation on using Microsoft Bookings on Microsoft's support site.
Be sure to explore all capabilities of Bookings before publishing your calendar. If you have any questions or concerns regarding Bookings, please contact your local IT or the OIT Help Desk.

" KB0019411 Rutgers Connect Microsoft Publisher End-of-Life "
End of Support October 1, 2026
Microsoft has announced that it will permanently retire Microsoft Publisher on October 1, 2026. After that date, Publisher will no longer be included in Microsoft 365 subscriptions, and support for existing versions will end.
While Publisher is not widely used across Rutgers, it is currently installed on a number of university-managed devices and has been launched by approximately 500 users over the past year. We are sharing this information now to ensure awareness well in advance of the retirement date.
Details
After October 1, 2026:
•	Publisher will be removed from Microsoft 365 installations.
•	Microsoft 365 subscribers will no longer be able to open or edit Publisher (.pub) files in the application.
Versions include:
•	Publisher for Microsoft 365
•	Publisher 2021 (see note)
•	Publisher 2019 (see note)
•	Publisher 2016
•	Publisher 2013
•	Publisher 2010
Note: Standalone versions (e.g.: "Publisher 2019", "Publisher 2021") may continue to function but will no longer receive updates or security fixes from Microsoft.
User preparation
Microsoft recommends converting existing .pub files to PDF or Word prior to October 2026. It is understood that file conversions may not fully preserve formatting or layout, and users should plan accordingly. 
Next steps
It's recommended that departmental IT begin identifying any supported users who may rely on Publisher so they can plan ahead. The Office of Information Technology has created documentation instructions for exporting Microsoft Publisher files that are in the .pub format to PDF or Word, as well as recommendations for Rutgers-supported alternate applications.

" KB0012512 Rutgers Connect Migrating Rutgers Connect Personal Data to ScarletMail "
Upon separation from the University, please arrange to transfer all Rutgers property (including electronic data) to the appropriate authority. For departing faculty and staff, the Offboarding Checklist may prove useful. 
After transferring all Rutgers data, you may find some amount of personally owned data remains. Examples of such data include personally-owned scholarly works and student coursework, as described in University Policy 50.3.7. You will not have access to this data on Rutgers Connect following your separation. However, as an alumni or retiree, you may be provided continuing service on ScarletMail. This document describes OIT's suggested method of moving data from a Rutgers Connect account to a ScarletMail account.
This procedure must be used exclusively on personally-owned data. Data classified as Restricted or Critical ePHI under Rutgers Information Classification Policy 70.1.2 must not be transferred to ScarletMail nor any other non-Rutgers system. Doing so may represent a violation of the Federal HIPAA Privacy/Security rules, State Privacy Laws, and/or University policies. Please prepare your data accordingly prior to the migration procedure.
Your Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator may have additional details regarding unit-level data practices. Please feel free to engage them with your questions or concerns.

•	Your ScarletMail account
•	A Microsoft Exchange Profile or an export of your Rutgers Connect account in a .PST file. View Microsoft's support article on How to Create a PST file.

•	Microsoft Outlook 2010, Microsoft Outlook 2013, Microsoft Outlook 2016, or Microsoft Outlook 2019
•	Windows 7, Windows 8, Windows 10, or Windows 11. MacOS is NOT supported
This tool will allow you to import mail, calendars, and personal contacts from your Rutgers Connect account to your ScarletMail account.

     Error! Filename not specified.

" KB0012611 Rutgers Connect Mobile device management policy "
Mobile Device Management for Office 365 has been enabled for all Rutgers Connect Accounts. Mobile Device Management (MDM) helps secure mobile devices to ensure compliance with University policies. While enrolling your device in MDM through the Company Portal App, you will see a notice stating that administrators will be allowed to make a number of changes to your device, but the University will not use those features, as they are beyond policy.
If you are associated with RBHS, review the Mobile Device Management policy for RBHS. 
The MDM policies that are currently in effect for all Rutgers staff and faculty are:
•	A password is required on the device. 
o	Google has set the minimum for personal devices to be a non-repeating, non-sequential 4 digit pin.
o	Apple has set the minimum for personal devices to be a 4 digit pin.
•	Jailbroken or rooted devices (devices that have had basic security measures stripped away from the operating system) will not work.
•	Managing email profile will be required.
•	Remotely wipe a mobile device if it is lost or stolen (this will not occur without the explicit consent of the device’s owner).
•	A device OS version that matches or exceeds the minimum supported version listed in the Office Suite Supported Versions article.
Instructions for enabling Mobile Device Management on iOS and Android devices can be found at the links below.
•	Enabling Mobile Device Management on Android Devices
•	Enabling Mobile Device Management on iOS Devices
There are known email applications that bypass MDM restrictions. These applications should not be used as they violate the Rutgers Connect MDM Standard. Below is a list of the currently known applications that are noncompliant:
•	CloudMagic
•	BlueMail
•	Newton
•	Typeapp
•	MyMail
•	SparkMail
•	EdisonMail
If you are leaving the university or no longer wish to have your device enabled to access Rutgers Connect on your mobile device, please remove the Intune Company Portal app from your device.
" KB0012612 Rutgers Connect Mobile device management policy for RBHS "
Mobile Device Management for Office 365 has been enabled for the Connect Accounts of those who have PHI flags. The PHI flag is in place to denote those who have access to Protected Health Information (PHI) and must abide by HIPAA regulations on how to store or send their email. Mobile Device Management (MDM) is a way to secure mobile devices so that they are compliant with the requirements of handling PHI. While enrolling your device in MDM through the Company Portal App, you will be prompted by a notice that states administrators will be allowed to make a number of changes to your device but the University will not utilize those features as they are beyond policy.
The MDM policies that are currently in effect for all staff who handle PHI data are:
•	Devices will be wiped after 10 sign-in failures
•	A password will be required on the device. 
o	For iOS, iPadOS, and Corporate Android devices: 
	The password must be at least 6 characters.
	The password must be alphanumeric with 2 character sets (including at least one special character).
o	For Personal and Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) Android devices: 
	Use either a password with at least 6 alphanumeric characters or a PIN with at least 8 digits.
	Repeating or ordered sequences of 4 or more characters or digits are blocked.
•	Devices will be locked after 15 minutes of inactivity.
•	Devices must have data encryption enabled. Apple devices (iOS devices) have built-in encryption that is automatically enabled but Android devices will need to enable encryption manually. This process is battery-intensive and may take up to an hour to complete, so make sure your device is plugged in while encrypting.
•	Jailbroken or rooted devices (devices with basic security measures stripped away from the operating system) will not work.
•	Managing email profile will be required.
•	A device OS version that matches or exceeds what's listed on the Office Suite Supported Versions article.
•	Removable storage on devices cannot be used.
Note: If your device utilizes a removable media device/removable storage (such as an SD card) the Help Desk advises that you copy the data to another location prior to enabling your device for MDM. Failure to properly copy your data prior to enabling your device may result in a loss of data.
Due to the implementation of MDM, IMAP has been turned off on both mobile and desktop devices for those who have access to PHI. This will require you to connect using Exchange when using your Connect account, which will enforce the MDM rules. You will need to access your Connect account using Outlook Web Access (OWA), Outlook, or a mobile device enrolled in MDM.
Instructions on how to enable iOS and Android devices for Mobile Device Management can be found in the links below.
•	Enabling Mobile Device Management on Android Devices
•	Enabling Mobile Device Management on iOS Devices
There are known mail applications that bypass the restrictions of MDM. These applications should not be used as they violate the Rutgers Connect MDM Standard. Below is a list of the currently known applications that are noncompliant:
•	CloudMagic
•	BlueMail
•	Newton
•	Typeapp
•	MyMail
•	SparkMail
If you are leaving the university or no longer wish to have your device enabled to access Rutgers Connect on your mobile device, please remove the Intune Company Portal app from your device.
" KB0018110 Rutgers Connect Mobile Device Supported Operating Systems for Rutgers Connect "
With each major update of a mobile device's Operating System (OS), Microsoft also updates the minimum supported version of OS's for the Office Suite. Devices below this threshold are no longer supported by Microsoft and their apps will not receive feature and/or security updates. To improve security and support, the University will be setting OS minimums that devices must maintain or they will be un-enrolled from our tenant. These minimums will be updated as new OS versions are released. These limits currently are:
•	iOS/iPadOS minimum OS: 18
•	Android minimum OS: 13
If you have a device below these limits, you will receive a notification on your device the next time it checks in. If an OS update is not applied to the device, the notification will come up again on day 7, 14, 21, and 28. If the you do not update by day 15, you will receive an email notification that your device needs to be updated. On day 30 your device will be un-enrolled from Intune Company portal and removed from the Rutgers tenant. This would be the same as if the you had manually un-registered your device from the Intune Company Portal.
iOS/iPadOS Notification
Error! Filename not specified.
Android Notification
Error! Filename not specified.
For any device that needs updating, either just OS or hardware, it's recommended to un-enroll the device from Intune Company Portal, follow your device manufacturers recommendations for back-ups, do all pending updates, then re-enroll the device with an updated version of the Intune Company Portal. If the device does not update to the minimum OS needed for mobile Office, the University can not guarantee that Microsoft publishes a suitable version of mobile Office apps for your OS.

" KB0013635 Rutgers Connect Office Suite Supported Versions "
For the best experience, use the most current build of any operating system and application specified below. Product functionality and feature availability may vary on older systems.
Microsoft 365 Apps
Windows 11, Windows Server 2025 until October 2029, and Windows Server 2022 until October 2026.  One of the three most recent versions of macOS. 
Microsoft Office 2024
Windows 11, Windows Server 2025, or Windows Server 2022. For ARM-based devices, Windows 11 is the minimum supported version of Windows OS. Office for Mac is supported on the three most recent versions of macOS.  Connections to Microsoft 365 services are supported while Office LTSC 2024 is in mainstream support, through October 2029.
Microsoft Office 2021
Windows 11, or Windows Server 2022. Office for Mac is supported on the three most recent versions of macOS.  Connections to Microsoft 365 services are supported while Office LTSC 2021 is in mainstream support, through October, 2026.
Microsoft Office 2019
Support for Office 2019 connections to Microsoft 365 services ended October 2023.
Microsoft Office 2016
Support for Office 2016 connections to Microsoft 365 services ended October 2023.
Mobile Office for iOS
Office for iPad and iPhone (including Outlook for iOS) is supported on the two most recent versions of iOS and iPadOS. When a new version of iOS or iPadOS is released, the Office Operating System requirement becomes the two most recent versions: the new version of iOS or iPadOS and the previous version. 
Mobile Office for Android
Office for Android (including Outlook for Android) can be installed on tablets and phones running the last four major versions of Android that have an ARM-based or Intel x86 processor.  When a new version of Android is released, the Office Operating System requirement becomes the four most recent versions: the new version of Android and the previous three versions.
More detailed information about Microsoft Office and it's apps (Access, Excel, OneNote, Outlook, PowerPoint, Publisher, Teams, and Word) may be found on Microsoft's website.

" KB0012617 Rutgers Connect OneDrive for Business "
OneDrive for Business is a feature of Rutgers Connect (Office 365) that lets you store, sync, and share your work files in the cloud. With OneDrive for Business, you can share and collaborate on work documents with co-workers.
Please note that OneDrive is designed to securely upload your documents to the cloud so you can access your data from any device. You may want to move your Desktop or My Documents folders to OneDrive to sync them with the cloud, but we recommend against uploading your entire hard drive. Attempting to sync system, program, and configuration files will unnecessarily consume your OneDrive quota and may affect OneDrive's ability to efficiently sync your important files.
When you store your files with OneDrive, you can:
•	Access and update files from anywhere on any device.
•	Manage your business files on the road.
•	Collaborate on documents with others at the same time.
•	Synchronize files from the cloud service to your desktop and work with them offline.
Instructions for setting up OneDrive on your computer can be found at the links below.
•	Setting up OneDrive for Business on Windows
•	Setting up OneDrive for Business on Mac
Find out more about OneDrive on Rutgers Connect. 
" KB0012618 Rutgers Connect OneDrive on Rutgers Connect "
Microsoft’s OneDrive is part of the Rutgers Connect suite and is available to all faculty, staff, students, and guests. OneDrive allows up to 5 terabytes of storage per user, including restricted data such as files containing protected health information (PHI). OneDrive supports all Windows, MacOS, Android*, iOS*, and Linux devices and has a full-featured web interface that can be used on other platforms. File sharing can be used to share information with anyone, as anonymous link sharing has been enabled.
Availability: All faculty, staff, students, and guests
Storage limit: 5 Terabytes
File size limit: 250 gigabytes
File limit: 30 million documents (300,000 limit recommended for sync performance)
Speed limits: Not documented (varies based on a number of factors; no issue has been experienced)
Access methods: Windows Client, MacOS Client, Android App*, Apple iOS App*, Linux, Web
Document versions: 500
PHI permitted: Yes
Integrated with Canvas: Yes
•	Content viewers must have an account: No
•	Instructors and viewers must add an appropriate email to Canvas settings: Yes
•	Content viewers must also use the same tenant: No
*Mobile device management required
To access OneDrive, navigate to Rutgers Connect, log in, and select Apps in the top left corner (nine dots) and then OneDrive.

" KB0012634 Rutgers Connect Recipient experience for encrypted emails in Connect "
Table of Contents
•	Encrypt or Encrypt-Only
•	Do Not Forward
•	Rutgers Connect – Confidential
•	Rutgers Connect – Confidential View Only
Encrypt or Encrypt-Only
If the sender chose Encrypt or Encrypt-Only, and the recipient is using the Outlook Web App (connect.rutgers.edu), Outlook, the Windows 10 Mail app, or Outlook for Android or iOS, the recipient will be able to read and reply to encrypted emails just like any other message. They will notice a banner at the top of the email that says "Encrypt: This message is encrypted. Recipients can’t remove encryption."
Error! Filename not specified.
If the sender is using another email service, such as Gmail (including ScarletMail) or Yahoo, they will receive a link to read the message in a secure window instead.
Error! Filename not specified.
If they are using the Outlook desktop application, they can click on the banner that says the message is encrypted and choose View Permissions to see detailed information about what they can do with the message.
Error! Filename not specified.
Do Not Forward
If the sender chose Do Not Forward and the recipient is using the Outlook Web App, Outlook, the Windows 10 Mail app, or Outlook for Android or iOS, the recipient will be able to read the email normally, but will see a message at the top that says "Do Not Forward: recipients can’t forward, print or copy content". As stated, they will be unable to forward, print or copy the email.
Error! Filename not specified.
As with the Encrypt option, non-Outlook users will receive a link to read the message in a secure window.
Error! Filename not specified.
Rutgers Connect – Confidential
If the sender chose Rutgers Connect – Confidential, and the recipient is using the Outlook Web App, Outlook, the Windows 10 Mail app, or Outlook for Android or iOS, they will be able to read the email normally, but will see a message at the top that says "Rutgers University – Confidential: This content is proprietary information intended for internal users only." They will be able to reply and modify the email, but will not be able to copy or print it. Users who are accessing their Rutgers Connect account through third-party apps, like Apple Mail, will receive a link to read the message in a secure window. Users of non-Rutgers email will be unable to view the message.
Error! Filename not specified.
Rutgers Connect – Confidential View Only
If the sender chose Rutgers Connect – Confidential View Only, and they are using the Outlook Web App, Outlook, the Windows 10 Mail app, or Outlook for Android or iOS, they will be able to read the email normally, but will see a message at the top that says "Rutgers University – Confidential: This content is proprietary information intended for internal users only. This content cannot be modified." You will be able to view the email, but will not be able to edit, copy or print it. Users who are accessing their Rutgers Connect account through third-party apps, like Apple Mail, will receive a link to read the message in a secure window. Users of non-Rutgers email will be unable to view the message.
Error! Filename not specified.

Text Box Linking	Good (Area Type)	Supports "Threaded Text" between shapes, but it’s less stable than InDesign for long documents and doesn't handle "Overset" text as gracefully.	
Adobe InDesign	Business Stationery & Operations	Excellent	Handles precise letterheads and business cards; supports interactive PDF forms for operations.

Object Nudging	Precision-Grade	Extremely precise nudging via arrow keys or the "Step and Repeat" function. Nudge by 0.001pt increments. Includes "Step and Repeat" for creating perfect grids of objects instantly.

Page Guides	Excellent	Features "New Guide Layout" which can instantly generate complex grids, columns, and gutters for your canvas.	
Personal & Event Design	Excellent	The best tool for digital art, photo collages, and "moody" event posters where the image is the star.

Back to top	Mail Merge	Not available (Native)	PowerPoint does not have a built-in Mail Merge feature. You would need to design in PowerPoint, export as an image, and then perform the merge in Word or InDesign.
Object Nudging	Excellent	Precise, 1-pixel nudge control using arrow keys. Holding Ctrl while nudging (Ctrl + Arrow) allows sub-pixel nudging for even finer precision. The "Smart Guides" (red dashed lines) are the best in the Microsoft suite and make alignment very intuitive.

Microsoft Word	Business Stationery & Operations	Best-in-Class	The absolute gold standard for letterheads, memos, and internal reports. It integrates perfectly with the rest of Rutgers' Outlook system.
Back to top	Mail Merge	Industry Leader	The most powerful and user-friendly mail merge available. It connects directly to Excel or Outlook contacts.

Professional Marketing	Moderate	Good for text-heavy newsletters or resumes, but poor for complex image-heavy brochures.	
Text Box Linking	Hidden Gem	Most people don't know Word can do this. You can create "Links" between text boxes so text flows from Box A to Box B.

     Error! Filename not specified.

" KB0012645 Rutgers Connect Rutgers Connect account audits "
Who can have a Rutgers Connect account?
According to Office of Information Technology guidelines, only the following classes of people are eligible to have Rutgers Connect accounts:
•	On-boarded (current and future) employees of Rutgers University
•	Current students that handle Protected Health Information (PHI), such as RBHS students
•	Professor Emeritus
The following groups of people are not automatically eligible for Rutgers Connect accounts:
•	Former employees (including teaching/graduate assistants who may still be students but are not actively working for Rutgers)
•	Employees of other organizations who are performing work at Rutgers
•	Students (current and future) who do not handle PHI
•	Alumni
•	Retirees
Students from other units may be eligible if the departments or divisions they work for wish to sponsor them. Additionally, Rutgers Connect accounts may be provided to Guests, who are individuals who are conducting University business and are directly associated with the University, but are not officially on the University’s payroll. Examples of guests include visiting professors/scholars, members of auxiliary groups, and others who are working on University business or affiliated with the University.
These guests and students may be eligible for a Rutgers Connect account if a department or division of Rutgers is willing to sponsor them. Please contact your Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator for details.
Recently hired employees may be on-boarded to payroll by departmental HR staff, even with a future start date. The Rutgers Connect account will then automatically be available. If full on-boarding is not possible, departmental on-boarding staff may use the Early Employee NetID form to request early provisioning from OIT.
Note: Most students, retirees, and alumni are not eligible for Rutgers Connect; however, these groups are automatically eligible for an account on Rutgers ScarletMail. Please see the ScarletApps page for information about opening ScarletMail accounts.
How can I keep my Rutgers Connect account?
We determine which accounts should be closed by comparing Rutgers Connect accounts with the active roles (e.g. Faculty or Staff) of NetIDs listed in the University’s OpenRegistry (OR) service, which is used as the basis for the Rutgers Online Directory. The OR may have some information which needs to be corrected.
If you have received an account closure notice and you believe that this is in error, please find the group you belong to in the appropriate subsection below (Current Employees, Students, Guests, Others) and follow the instructions there.
Current Employees
You may not be listed in the OR as a current employee. To check this, go to the Search for People tool and search for your name. Review each result if you get more than one. If your name does not appear, contact your department’s Human Resources person.
When your entry appears, review the information there. If it is incorrect, contact your department’s Human Resources person.
After your department’s Human Resources person has corrected your record, your department’s Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator can verify that your account is no longer subject to closure.
Students
OIT cannot permit prior students (such as students on leave and alumni) access to Rutgers Connect, as the system contains Restricted data such as Protected Health Information (PHI). Students who are still in need of a non-PHI email account may use ScarletMail.
If you are a current student, first verify your status in OR. To check this, go to the Search for People tool and search for your name. Review each result if you get more than one. If your name does not appear, please inquire about your registration via One Stop.
When your entry appears, review the information there. If it is incorrect, please inquire about your registration via One Stop.
After you have corrected your course registration(s), your Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator can verify that your account is no longer subject to closure.
Guests
Guests will have to determine with their sponsor if Rutgers Connect, ScarletMail, or even no Rutgers email account (for example, using a home institution’s email service) is appropriate for their needs.
If you are affiliated with Rutgers but not actually employed full-time by Rutgers, you may request a guest account. Have a sponsor at the department you are working with go to the Guest Account site, and submit a request for you, which will be sent to our Accounts Office for processing. NOTE: A domain administrator within your department must activate a Connect account for you.
Every year, you must renew your guest account. You will be notified when the time to renew your account arrives (30 days prior to the expiration of the account).
Your Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator can assist your sponsor with submitting a Guest Account request and creating your Rutgers Connect account, if necessary.
Others
Retirees and alumni are automatically entitled to an account on Rutgers ScarletMail.
If you do not fit into any of the above categories, you may want to try contacting a department at Rutgers related to the work you do and ask if they would be willing to sponsor a Guest account for you.
We have no mechanism for people no longer associated with Rutgers to pay a fee and thus keep their accounts. These people should be able to pay for a full account on any number of Internet Service Providers (ISPs) or obtain a free email account from various web services. Rutgers cannot recommend one such group over another.
What is the typical account audit timeline?
Once an account is found to be ineligible for Connect:
•	On day one, i.e., same day found to be ineligible: The account is sent an email notification.
•	On day seven, i.e., approximately one week later: The account is locked out of Connect.
•	On day thirty-five, i.e., approximately 5 weeks later: The account is deleted from Connect.
If the account is found to be eligible for Connect at any time prior to deletion, the account will exit the audit.
Like all Rutgers NetID services, Rutgers Connect is subject to OIT NetID authentication processes. These practices may lock your Rutgers NetID – including Rutgers Connect access – on a different timeline. See the off-boarding process article for details about NetID authentication off-boarding. Please note that recent students in the “grace period” status described on that site are ineligible for the Rutgers Connect service. However, OIT will maintain data for the full duration of the “grace period” – the “day thirty-five" deletion does not apply in this case.
What should I do before the account is closed?
If you will be losing your Rutgers Connect account, you may want to take some of the following steps.
•	Use the Manage Email Addresses function to ensure you continue to receive Rutgers email. For example, retirees and alumni may be entitled to continuing email service on ScarletMail. They can set that as their delivery address and consider Migrating Rutgers Connect Personal Data to ScarletMail if appropriate.
•	Contact the IT staff in your department to determine the correct protocol for the data (email, contacts, and calendar) in your account. Departments that handle PHI or other sensitive data may have procedures put in place for security.
•	Notify your regular correspondents, mailing lists, etc., about your change of address. We cannot forward mail from a deleted account to another address.
•	You may want to use the “automatic reply” feature (available in the Settings after logging in at https://connect.rutgers.edu) to set up an automatic response, telling correspondents of the account’s eventual closure. Remember that the automatic reply feature will no longer work for you once your account has been fully deleted.
•	If you have it configured, remove your Work Hours and Location on your calendar. 
•	You will lose access to your Office 365 data once your account is deleted, so you will want to save your OneDrive for Business files to another location. Please contact your local IT staff to assist with this process.
What happens after the account is closed?
After your account is closed, you will lose access to your Rutgers Connect account. Your account will still receive email and any Office 365 applications associated with your account should still function as expected; however, you will no longer be able to sign in to the account.
Approximately 4 weeks after your account is closed, your Rutgers Connect account will be deleted.
After an account is deleted, you will no longer be able to access Office 365 services like email or OneDrive for Business. Your Office applications will move into a read-only, reduced functionality mode and display Unlicensed Product notifications.
Any e-mail addressed to such an account will be returned to the sender (“bounced”) with an automatic message of the type “Access denied”.
For further assistance
If you have questions about any of the above, you can send an email to help@oit.rutgers.edu or contact the OIT Help Desk.
" KB0012665 Rutgers Connect Sending Encrypted Email in Outlook "
Table of Contents
•	How to Encrypt an Email
•	Encrypt Options 
o	Encrypt
o	Do Not Forward
o	Rutgers Connect – Confidential
o	Rutgers Connect – Confidential View Only
o	Keyword Triggered
•	Outlook Application
Office 365's Office Message Encryption (OME) provides you the ability to customize the level of protection for any specific email you choose to encrypt. You can choose to encrypt the email, ensuring it is received exclusively by your intended recipient, or to limit their ability to forward it to others. For messages that require the greatest amount of security, you can choose to allow the email to only be viewed by or forwarded to other Rutgers Connect users, or even limit the Rutgers Connect recipient to view the email and be unable to copy, print, forward, or otherwise interact with the message. These options will be described in more detail later.
How to Encrypt an Email
Navigate to Rutgers Connect and log in. You can use these functions by clicking the Options tab on the ribbon, then clicking the Encrypt button at the top of your email in the Outlook Web App.
Error! Filename not specified.
In the Outlook Web App, when you click Protect, a banner appears at the top of your email that says "Do Not Forward: Recipients can read this message, but they can’t forward, print, or copy content." It will also include options to change the permission level or remove the protection altogether.
Error! Filename not specified.
If you select the option to change the permission level, you will see four options.
Error! Filename not specified.
Error! Filename not specified.
Encrypt Options
Encrypt
If you choose Encrypt, the message's contents will be encrypted. You can learn more about encryption here, but at a very basic level, you can imagine this as your message being converted into a secret code, with only authorized users (your intended message recipient) having the key to decrypt that encoded text back into your original message.
When you choose Encrypt, the recipient can do whatever they want with the message once they receive it. They can copy text from the message, print it, save it to their computer, reply to it, or forward it to other users. Encryption adds a layer of security that ensures your intended recipient is the only one who can receive your message – but it does not control what they can do with it once they have.
Do Not Forward
If you want a little bit more control over the message you are sending, you can choose the Do Not Forward option. This option encrypts the message as described above and also prevents the user from copying, printing, or forwarding its contents.
Rutgers Connect – Confidential
Choosing this option will only allow the message to be sent to other Rutgers Connect users. It is similar to Encrypt in that, while the message is protected, the recipient can still save, reply to, and forward it. It may only be forwarded to other Rutgers Connect users.
Rutgers Connect – Confidential View Only
This is the most restrictive option. If you choose this option, the recipient – who must be a Rutgers Connect user – will be able to view the message only. They will not be able to reply, forward, copy, or edit the message.
Keyword Triggered
For backward compatibility with our previous encryption service, Zix Corporation, any message containing the keyword "ZIXSECURE" in the subject or body and leaving Rutgers Connect will have OME encryption applied to it. OIT does not recommend using keywords to force encryption. The keyword feature has been retained for specialized cases and may be removed completely in the future, as it is being replaced by OME's encryption features.
Outlook Application
In the Outlook application, which can be installed locally on your computer for more robust email management, you can find the option with the Encrypt button when you select Options.
Error! Filename not specified.
From Outlook, once you click Encrypt you will see a message stating "Encrypt Only – This message is encrypted." You can change the permission level by clicking the small arrow to the right of the Encrypt button.
Error! Filename not specified.

" KB0012689 Rutgers Connect SharePoint roles and permission levels "
SharePoint offers default and custom permission levels to better manage user roles on specific sites. Below is a breakdown of common out-of-the-box permission levels and their intended roles.
Permission Level	Role
Read	•	Read and download site content
•	Browse site content
•	Search site content
•	Request higher access level
Contribute	•	All rights and responsibilities of the above role
•	Create, edit and delete list items and documents
Edit	•	All rights and responsibilities of the above roles
•	Can add, edit and delete lists
Design	•	All rights and responsibilities of the above roles
•	Create/Edit libraries
•	Change page structure and visual design
•	Add/Edit web parts
Full Control	•	All rights and responsibilities of the above roles
•	Administer permissions
 
These permission levels are collections of individual user permissions and can vary depending on the SharePoint template being used. The ones above are just some of the most common you will find on most sites. It is important to note that these are just collections of permissions; in order for them to be effective, they need to be applied to permission groups on the SharePoint site. SharePoint sites by default come with the following groups that have one of the above permission levels applied to them:
 
Permission Group	Permission Level
site-name Visitors	•	Read
site-name Members	•	Edit
site-name Owners	•	Full Control
 
As an example, a Teams-connected SharePoint site will have the site members' permission group populated with the 365 group's members, and the site owners' permission group will be populated with the 365 group's owners.
Visit the SharePoint website for additional information regarding sharing files, folders, and sites in SharePoint Online.
" KB0012703 Rutgers Connect Types of SharePoint sites "
Microsoft SharePoint offers a wide variety of sites to fulfill business objectives ranging from document storage to communicating department initiatives. Below is an outline for various SharePoint sites and their unique advantages.
Table of Contents
•	Team Sites 
o	Site Header
o	Left-hand Navigation and Search Pane
o	Overview
•	Communication Sites 
o	Topic Site Design
o	Showcase Site Design
o	Overview
•	Hub Sites 
o	Overview
•	Additional Resources about SharePoint Online Sites
Team Sites
Team sites allow members to collaborate on projects, events, or ideas by connecting them to the content, information, and web apps they need. On a team site home page, you can view links to valuable team files, web apps, and pages, as well as view recent site changes in the activity feed. Team sites are integrated by default within a wide range of Microsoft collaboration tools, such as Microsoft Planner and Microsoft Teams.
Error! Filename not specified.
Site Header
At the top of the team site, you will see a header with the site name, site logo, and whether the site is public (anyone in the organization can view) or private (only specific members can view). Site members with edit permissions will also see a “New” button that allows them to add a new list, document library, page, news post, or web app.
Error! Filename not specified.
Left-hand Navigation and Search Pane
At the top left of the site, you will see a search box where you can find files stored on the team site. Under the search box, you will see links to the default team document library, team OneNote notebook, site pages, site contents, site recycle bin, and custom links.
Error! Filename not specified.
Overview
Best for: Central location for team collaboration and document storage.
Permissions: Includes Office 365 group permissions, as well as default SharePoint group and permission levels.
Content Authors: All members who can create and edit content are content authors.
Availability: Can be created by the site owner or administrator as a site collection or subsite.
Use Cases: 
•	Project team working together to share ideas and manage tasks
•	Team storing important documents for current projects
Communication Sites
Communication sites are used to share information in a visually compelling format, featuring news posts, reports, events, statuses, and lists. These sites are great for displaying information to a broad audience, with a few members contributing to the content. When creating a team site, you can start with a blank site or choose a template (showcase or topic) site design that comes with a default set of web parts.
Topic Site Design
The Topic site design focuses on sharing important information, such as news and events, regarding a subject.
Error! Filename not specified.
Showcase Site Design
The Showcase site design focuses on effectively sharing information, such as product or team images.
Error! Filename not specified.
Overview
Best for: Showcasing content, including announcements, articles, services, and people, effectively.
Permissions: Default SharePoint permission levels.
Content Authors: A small number of authors and a larger number of viewers.
Availability: Can be created by the site owner or the SharePoint administrator only as a site collection.
Use Cases: 
•	Site showcasing new department initiative.
•	Intranet site for the HR department, including news posts from various employees.
Hub Sites
Hub sites are used to showcase, connect, and organize a wide variety of related sites into a central site. By connecting a family of team and communication sites, discovering related content, such as news and various site activities, becomes easier. Sites associated with a SharePoint hub site will have a hub site navigation bar added to the top of the site.
Error! Filename not specified.
Overview
Best for: Central site used to display and navigate to related team and communication sites.
Permissions: Default SharePoint permission levels.
Content Authors: The hub site owner defines the hub navigation and theme. Hub site members create content on the hub site. Site owners and members of sites associated with the parent hub site create content on their respective sites.
Availability: Can be created by a Global administrator or a SharePoint administrator.
Use Cases: 
•	University hub that provides navigation to different departments, such as Accounting, Information Technology, and Finance.
•	A specific hub site that groups the communication and team sites for a specific location (Busch Campus)
•	A sales hub that provides enterprise resources to the sales organization and connects them to various communication sites
Although SharePoint sites allow for advanced customization based on a variety of needs, there are limitations to the content management system. Below are a few to keep in mind:
•	Sites are limited to being shared internally among the organization, with the correct permission level to view.
•	Embedding custom scripts to alter site behavior or appearance is not supported.
•	Resizing of imported images is currently not supported.
•	News posts can only feature a single author.
•	Adding images to text boxes is not supported.
•	For storage of confidential documents, please use Perceptive Content (formerly ImageNow)
•	Teams chats cannot be embedded on SharePoint pages.

" KB0012708 Rutgers Connect Using Scheduling Poll to Schedule Meetings "
As of December 2023, the FindTime add-in has been retired. Scheduling Poll is the replacement feature and is built directly into Outlook as a native feature. 
The new Scheduling Poll feature, in replacement of the FindTime add-in, is used to schedule meetings via polling. The organizer can send multiple time options through the Scheduling Poll feature and minimize the back-and-forth emails about scheduling. 
The Scheduling Poll feature is currently available to users of Microsoft 365 Apps for business or enterprise plans that include Exchange Online. It is currently supported for GCC tenants, excluding GCC High.
A meeting organizer is required to have a mailbox in Microsoft 365 Exchange Online to be able to use the Scheduling Poll feature, while anyone with a valid email address can be an attendee in a meeting that utilizes the Scheduling Poll feature for polling. This feature is not available to organizers with mailboxes on an Exchange On-Premises server.
Access Scheduling Poll
1.	Navigate and log in to your Rutgers Connect account. 
2.	Create a new email or select an email to reply to.
3.	List required attendees for the meeting in the To field and optional attendees in the Cc field.
4.	Select Scheduling poll in the Message tab, which is displayed in the Simplified Ribbon or Classic Ribbon. 

Error! Filename not specified.

Error! Filename not specified.
5.	Create a new meeting event or select an existing event to edit it.
6.	List required attendees in the Invite attendees field and click Optional to add optional attendees.
7.	Select Scheduling poll in the Event tab, which is displayed in the Simplified Ribbon or Classic Ribbon. 
Create a Scheduling Poll
The organizer can send multiple time options through the Scheduling Poll and minimize the back-and-forth emails about scheduling. 
1.	Select the meeting settings.
o	View all your polls: Click this link to view and manage all the polls created by you.
o	Time zone: Select the time zone dropdown menu to change the time zone for the meeting.
o	Duration: Select a meeting duration from the list.
o	Meeting hours: Check to limit suggested meeting times to workdays and working hours only.
o	Date Picker: The date picker will allow you to pick different dates to see time availability. You can add times from different dates to a poll. Alternatively, you can use the left and right arrow buttons to go to the previous or next day and use the calendar icon (between the arrow buttons) to jump back to today.
2.	Scheduling Poll looks through the attendees' schedules (if available) and suggests a list of suitable meeting times. Factors used to determine the best options include how many attendees are free, how many required vs. optional attendees are free, and whether conflicted attendees have tentative or busy commitments on their calendar. 
o	People Icons: Hovering over the person icon will show participants’ availability and whether they are required or optional.  
	Underlined: Organizer
	Green: Available
	Red: Busy
	Purple: Out of Office
	Gray: Unknown
o	Expand/Collapse button: Will allow you to see a detailed list of participants’ availability and whether they are required or optional for a given time suggestion.
3.	Select a few suitable meeting times. The Next button will be enabled if you select one or more options.
4.	Select Next. You will be presented with the list of selected times and poll settings before you can finish creating the poll.

Error! Filename not specified.
1.	To delete any selected meeting times, click the delete icon in the Selected times list. 
2.	Enter meeting location if needed. 
3.	Select the Online Meeting check box to disable its default. 
4.	To view more options, use the Manage poll settings expand/collapse button.  
	Schedule when attendees reach consensus: A calendar event is automatically scheduled if all required attendees have voted in favor of a specific time option. If multiple options are available, the earliest option will be scheduled.
	Hold selected times on my calendar: A tentative event is placed on your calendar for each time option you propose. All holds are removed when the meeting is scheduled or the poll is canceled.
	Notify me about poll updates: You’ll receive an email each time an attendee votes. The message includes the current poll status and an option to schedule.
	Require attendees to verify their identity: To help prevent anonymous voting, attendees will be required to authenticate before voting.
	Lock poll for attendees: Attendees will not be able to suggest new times or edit other attendees.
5.	Select Create poll. Scheduling Poll inserts the poll details into your email body, which includes a link to the voting page and a link to all the polls you’ve created so far.
6.	Select Send to send the email and start the voting process.
For further information on Scheduling Poll voting, the organizer dashboard, or auto-scheduling, visit the Microsoft Support page for more Scheduling Poll articles.
